articles.title: Eli Manning warns his nephew Arch following the heated controversy over laughing at an AI video: “They’re not your friends”
articles.standfirst: The Super Bowl champion offers strong words of advice to the Texas Longhorns star.
articles.summary: The Super Bowl champion offers strong words of advice to the Texas Longhorns star.
articles.body:
Arch Manning has received some timely advice from his uncle Eli after a bizarre media controversy overshadowed Texas Longhorns ’ dramatic victory over the Ohio State Buckeyes earlier this month. The young quarterback sparked backlash after revealing that he had laughed at an AI-generated video appearing to show coach Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe .

Arch later apologized to Rowe via Instagram Stories, but the incident offered a lesson about how quickly a seemingly harmless joke can spread and take on a life of its own and Eli is keen to drill the lesson home. “He'll have to figure out that media on his own,” Manning indirectly said to Arch, via Front Office Sports. “And a lot of it is just kind of growing pains. “You feel like media's your pal, you relax with them a little bit, you try to be funny, and then they can take it and run. You gotta be careful.”

Arch Manning has tough night as Longhorns brush UTSA Roadrunners aside

Arch then endured a difficult night on the college football field despite Texas defeating the UTSA Roadrunners 30-6, as he finished 16-of-32 passing for 161 yards in the Longhorns ’ final game before SEC play. The sophomore quarterback did connect with Cam Coleman twice for touchdowns, but he struggled to find consistency and absorbed several heavy hits while Texas dealt with shaky pass protection. The performance came after Arch had produced a spectacular fourth-quarter comeback against Ohio State , throwing Texas back into the game before the Longhorns completed a 24-23 victory. Texas improved to 3-0 with the win over UTSA , but the quarterback acknowledged afterward that his performance was not good enough ahead of the much tougher schedule ahead in the race to the College Football Playoffs . Arch 's night included several missed opportunities, with the quarterback missing open receivers and overthrowing others while repeatedly scrambling away from pressure, with his helmet knocked off following a heavy collision in the second quarter. The UTSA defense that continued to pressure the quarterback, but it was a different story on the other side of the ball as the Longhorns ' defense continued its impressive start by limiting their opponent to 143 total yards and no touchdowns. Arch and Texas now turn their attention to Tennessee on Saturday, September 26 , with the quarterback facing a significantly tougher test against the Volunteers .

articles.title: Lane Kiffin's LSU problems keep mounting: Criminal investigation launched for Tigers player's alleged sexual assault
articles.standfirst: A concerning situation from last year is rearing its ugly head.
articles.summary: A concerning situation from last year is rearing its ugly head.
articles.body:
Last weekend did not go as Lane Kiffin had it planned. Making a return to Ole Miss , this time as a villain of the Rebels, Kiffin watched as his LSU Tigers lost the game 32-24 on a fourth quarter touchdown from Trinidad Chambliss - the star quarterback he helped recruit to Ole Miss before leaving.

It was definitely a hostile environment for Kiffin, although it wasn't nearly as bad as some expected. Now, Kiffin's attention must shift to getting LSU back on track . A bounce-back won't come easy, as No. 23 Texas A&M are coming to visit. As if Kiffin didn't have enough to stress about, there's now a concerning legal situation unfolding with an LSU player .

Criminal investigation underway for alleged sexual assault committed by LSU football player

According to WAFB Channel 9 of Baton Rouge, Louisiana, a criminal investigation is now underway for an alleged sexual assault involving a Tigers football player . This was confirmed by the East Baton Rouge District Attorney's office on Tuesday.

As of right now, the identity of the player that's been accused is unknown . Whether that player is currently on the team right now, is also not known. No charges have been made yet . Regardless, it's bad optics for a football program that would like to avoid any more negative PR going forward.

The sexual assault incident took place in 2025 . The alleged victim posted a detailed account of the incident on her TikTok page (user Kendall Danielle) on September 14, claiming that an LSU football player raped her. This story is developing.

articles.title: “Really bad”: The terrifying reality facing the Texas Longhorns that could shatter Arch Manning’s championship dreams
articles.standfirst: A dangerous road test awaits Texas as Tennessee looks to expose cracks in the Longhorns
articles.summary: A dangerous road test awaits Texas as Tennessee looks to expose cracks in the Longhorns
articles.body:
Texas ’ perfect start has done little to erase one uncomfortable question: can the Longhorns finally prove they can win away from Austin?

After opening the season 3-0 at home, Steve Sarkisian’s team now heads to Neyland Stadium for one of its toughest tests yet, bringing a troubling road history into the matchup with Tennessee.

CBS analyst Bud Elliott recently highlighted that issue, describing Texas as “legitimately bad” on the road under Sarkisian . The concern isn’t difficult to understand.

Last season, the Longhorns lost 29-21 at Florida and were beaten 35-10 by Georgia. Their two road victories, meanwhile, came against Kentucky and Mississippi State, with both games requiring overtime.

The Kentucky escape was particularly revealing. Texas managed just 179 total yards, while Arch Manning completed only 12 of 27 passes for 132 yards. The Longhorns ultimately escaped with a 16-13 victory, but the performance exposed how quickly their offense can become vulnerable when playing away from home.

Elliott also believes Manning hasn’t quite made the leap many expected. The quarterback has shown plenty of talent, but his production has fluctuated during the opening weeks of the season.

“Arch has been…he has not taken the jump that I think we expected him to take based on how he played down the stretch last year,” wrote Elliott.

Through Texas’ first three games, Manning went from throwing for 305 yards and four touchdowns against Texas State to 195 yards and one touchdown against Ohio State, followed by 164 yards and two scores against UTSA.

Those numbers don’t erase his ability, but they do raise questions about whether he can consistently deliver at the level expected from one of college football’s biggest names.

Tennessee’s pressure plan could decide the night

That issue could become even more important against Tennessee. Volunteers secondary coach Anthony Poindexter has already identified Texas’ vertical passing game as a major challenge, praising Manning’s arm talent while emphasizing the number of weapons surrounding him.

Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman give Manning explosive options on the outside, while Texas also has dangerous tight ends and running backs capable of contributing in the passing game. That creates a difficult strategic problem for Tennessee.

If the Volunteers can pressure Manning with four defenders, they’ll be able to keep more players in coverage and potentially limit those explosive plays. But if Tennessee has to send five or six rushers consistently, Texas could find favorable one-on-one matchups for its receivers.

There’s also been increasing attention on Manning away from the field. Following criticism surrounding a viral AI-generated video incident and a separate media controversy involving Sarkisian, Manning has become noticeably more reserved during media sessions.

His recent answers have been brief, offering reporters little opportunity to generate another viral moment.

That won’t matter once the game kicks off. Neyland Stadium will present Manning with an environment unlike anything he’s experienced this season, and Texas’ response could reveal whether its early success can travel.

The challenge for Manning is to turn flashes of elite ability into sustained production against a defense preparing specifically for Texas’ passing attack.

If Texas wants its championship ambitions to remain realistic, proving it can perform under pressure away from Austin may be just as important as anything Manning does with the ball.

articles.title: Donald Trump will attend Texas-Tennessee showdown to watch Arch Manning in historic first regular-season meeting
articles.summary: It is no secret that President Donald Trump likes to show up at the biggest sports stages. He was at Super Bowl 59 between the Kansas City Chiefs and Philadelphia Eagles and at Game 3 of this year’s NBA Finals in New York, both firsts for a sitting president at those events.
articles.body:
It is no secret that President Donald Trump likes to show up at the biggest sports stages. He was at Super Bowl 59 between the Kansas City Chiefs and Philadelphia Eagles and at Game 3 of this year’s NBA Finals in New York, both firsts for a sitting president at those events.

Now the White House has confirmed he will be in Knoxville on Saturday for No. 14 Tennessee against No. 1 Texas , a report first floated by Clay Travis. It will be Trump’s first college football game since last winter’s national championship, when Indiana beat Miami. Kickoff is noon ET on ABC.

Both teams are 3-0. The Longhorns are 3-0 after knocking off Ohio State, and Arch Manning will play his first true road game of the year in front of more than 100,000 fans at Neyland Stadium.

First Regular-Season Meeting Draws GameDay and a Sold-Out Neyland

This is the first regular-season meeting between the Longhorns and Volunteers . They have only played three times before, all in the Cotton Bowl: Tennessee won in 1951 , Texas in 1953 and 1969 . The building is sold out for Tennessee’s 30th straight sellout.

Capacity is 101,915, and Texas coach Steve Sarkisian already called Neyland “the loudest stadium in the country.”

On the field it is the game of the weekend, even with six AP-ranked matchups on the same day for the first time since 2023.

ESPN’s College GameDay , with Pat McAfee and the rest of the crew, will be on campus, and there is talk Trump could appear as a guest picker, which would be a first for a U.S. president on the show.

Peyton Manning is also expected to be in Knoxville to watch his nephew play against his alma mater. Saturday will tell how Arch and Texas handle a hostile road opener with the president watching from a heavily secured box.

articles.title: No re-entry, no exceptions: Trump's presence changes the rules for the Tennessee vs. Texas game and forces the Secret Service to take control
articles.standfirst: The presidential visit is adding unprecedented security measures to an already massive SEC showdown
articles.summary: The presidential visit is adding unprecedented security measures to an already massive SEC showdown
articles.body:
Neyland Stadium was already preparing for a massive Saturday when President Donald Trump’s expected appearance added an entirely new dimension to the Tennessee-Texas showdown.

No. 1 Texas is scheduled to visit No. 13 Tennessee on Sept. 26 for a noon ET SEC opener, with ESPN’s College GameDay also setting up in Knoxville. Trump’s attendance means fans won’t experience a routine game day, however.

University officials are warning spectators to arrive considerably earlier because enhanced security measures will be in place throughout the stadium and surrounding campus.

All Neyland Stadium gates will open at 9 a.m., three hours before kickoff. The Secret Service will conduct enhanced screening at every entrance, while additional checkpoints and verification procedures are expected around the venue.

Fans have been told to have mobile tickets ready before reaching the gates to help move the large crowds through security.

One of the biggest changes is the re-entry policy. Once a ticket has been scanned, fans won’t be permitted to leave and return to the stadium. That makes planning particularly important for anyone arriving early or expecting to move in and out of the venue during the day.

The clear-bag policy will also remain in effect, alongside additional Secret Service restrictions. Aerosols, flammable liquids, pepper spray, selfie sticks, glass and certain containers are among the prohibited items.

There won’t be storage facilities at the stadium for restricted belongings, so fans could be forced to return items to their vehicles before entering.

A football spectacle under an unusual security operation

The security arrangements are arriving as Knoxville prepares for one of the most anticipated games of the season. Both teams are unbeaten entering the matchup, while Texas remains No. 1 nationally and Tennessee is ranked in the top 15.

The game is also notable because it’s the first regular-season meeting between the schools. Their previous three encounters all came in the Cotton Bowl, with Texas holding a 2-1 advantage.

The atmosphere will be amplified by College GameDay, which will broadcast from Ayres Hall before moving inside Neyland Stadium for its final hour ahead of kickoff. Tennessee will also bring back its “Checker Neyland” tradition, turning the stadium into an alternating orange-and-white display.

Outside the stadium, fans should expect heavier vehicle and pedestrian traffic, possible temporary road closures and altered walking routes. Officials are advising visitors to allow additional travel time both before and after the game.

Trump’s presence also adds a broader political dimension to an already high-profile sporting weekend. His administration has taken an interest in college athletics policy, while the bipartisan Protect College Sports Act has recently advanced in the Senate, addressing areas including NIL compensation, scholarships, healthcare and transfer rules.

The immediate priority is much simpler for tens of thousands of fans heading to Knoxville, and that is to get there early, travel light and be prepared to stay inside once the ticket is scanned.

articles.body:
The Colorado football program made a drastic decision by removing several players from its roster for “conduct detrimental to the team,” a move confirmed by head coach Deion Sanders during his weekly press conference on Tuesday.

Although the details behind the disciplinary action have not yet been revealed, Sanders made it clear that the decision was not based solely on what happened after the Buffaloes’ 41-7 loss to Northwestern last Saturday.

Following the disappointing road defeat, the coach expressed his frustration, saying he could not understand how some players could take the loss lightly while he was walking behind them toward the locker room.

“It’s never one [thing],” Sanders said Tuesday during his news conference. “I’m one of the most loving and giving and forgiving men you could ever meet, but when you start having conduct detrimental to the team, you don’t care about the team, you care about you, and I have a problem with that. A year ago, I didn’t put my foot down in it enough. It lingered a little bit. Then, it imploded.”

“I’m not doing that anymore.”

After Sanders’ comments, the Colorado program released a statement clarifying that “any potential roster changes have not been finalized” and that it would provide an official roster update later this week.

The internal situation surrounding the Buffaloes was also shaken by another controversy involving safety Ben Finneseth, who apologized for comments captured on video before the matchup against Northwestern, which was played at the opponent’s temporary home stadium.

In the footage, Finneseth criticized the venue’s facilities, saying the stadium “sucks” and comparing the atmosphere to a “library” because of the lack of energy.

The player later acknowledged his mistake and apologized.

“It was childish; it was a stupid thing that I said. It won’t happen again,” Finneseth told reporters, according to The Athletic. “The way I handled it was horrible. I promise you guys it will not happen again and it’ll be much more mature moving forward.”

Colorado enters this week with a 2-1 record and will look to bounce back on Saturday when it faces Baylor in its first game of the season against a Big 12 Conference opponent.

articles.title: What happens if Donald Trump decides to go to the bathroom during the Texas vs. Tennessee game?
articles.standfirst: Trump’s movements inside Neyland Stadium could create an unusual communication issue for both teams
articles.summary: Trump’s movements inside Neyland Stadium could create an unusual communication issue for both teams
articles.body:
President Donald Trump’s presence at Saturday’s Texas-Tennessee matchup could create an unusual sideline problem, and it has nothing to do with the action on the field.

Trump is expected to attend the highly anticipated college football clash at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, where No. 1 Texas will face No. 14 Tennessee.

His appearance will bring increased security around the venue, but Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian has revealed that the president’s movements inside the stadium could also affect how the teams communicate during the game.

In particular, the communication systems used by coaches and players can be switched off when Trump enters, leaves or changes locations within the stadium.

That could mean a seemingly routine trip to the restroom might briefly leave coaches without their usual headset connection.

Sarkisian discussed the unusual situation during a news conference Thursday, explaining that communication between coaches, as well as coach-to-player communication, is cut whenever the president moves around the venue.

“The one thing that you have to be aware of when the president goes to any game is that any time he enters the stadium or leaves the stadium, or changes locations within the stadium, they cut all communication,” Sarkisian said.

The Texas coach also stressed that the teams won't necessarily receive advance notice before the communication systems are disconnected.

That creates an extra wrinkle for coaches trying to make adjustments during a game. If Trump suddenly changes locations during an important drive, the coaching staff could find itself temporarily unable to communicate through its normal headset system.

Trump’s movements could cause surprise communication blackouts

Sarkisian said he has already experienced the issue at another major college football game. He noted that similar communication interruptions occurred during the national championship matchup between Indiana and Miami while Trump was in attendance.

As a result, Texas will need to be prepared for the possibility of operating without its normal communications. Tennessee could face the same situation, making contingency plans particularly important for both coaching staffs.

It's also unclear exactly how long an individual communication blackout will last or how often it could happen during Saturday's game. Much will depend on whether Trump remains in one location or moves around the venue.

His visit is expected to affect spectators, too. Fans have been encouraged to arrive early because enhanced Secret Service screening and additional security measures could lead to longer lines and delays when entering Neyland Stadium.

There had also been questions about whether Trump would make an appearance on ESPN’s College GameDay before kickoff. However, he isn't expected to join the pregame show or serve as its guest picker. That role is set to go to Knoxville native Johnny Knoxville.

If Trump decides to make a bathroom trip during the Texas-Tennessee game, the president won't be stopping play. But his movement could briefly silence the headsets, leaving coaches to rely on their backup plans until communication is restored.

articles.title: LSU coach looks to Sam Leavitt after loss: “Everybody wants to blame the quarterback”
articles.standfirst: Kiffin shifts focus to pass protection amid criticism of Leavitt
articles.summary: Kiffin shifts focus to pass protection amid criticism of Leavitt
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin isn’t putting LSU’s loss to Ole Miss solely on Sam Leavitt.

The Tigers fell 32-24 in Oxford on September 19, handing Kiffin his first loss as LSU’s head coach against his former program. Leavitt attracted plenty of criticism afterward, particularly for his struggles during the first half and his performance on LSU’s final possession.

On Thursday, Kiffin defended his quarterback during The Lane Kiffin Show, pointing instead to problems in front of him.

“Well, we’ve got to play more consistently in the offensive line. You know, in the pass protection, Everybody wants to blame the quarterback,” Kiffin said.

“But when the quarterback can’t set his feet, or he’s getting hit early, especially on the road in the SEC, you know, he’s not the first quarterback to have numbers like that.

“They happen. So, a lot of that’s what happens in front, so we can step into throws and make the throws, and so that’s part of it.”

That context mattered against Ole Miss. Leavitt completed 16 of 27 passes for 153 yards and a touchdown, while adding 63 rushing yards and another score. LSU trailed 24-7 at halftime before mounting a comeback and eventually tying the game.

The quarterback still had difficult moments. Late in the contest, Leavitt missed tight end Zach Grace near the goal line. A fourth-down pass was then tipped and intercepted, ending LSU’s opportunity to complete the comeback.

The criticism has been significant. Skip Bayless questioned Leavitt’s pocket play following the defeat, while ESPN’s Jordan Rodgers argued that the quarterback needed to get the ball out of his hands faster. Those comments have added to the attention surrounding LSU’s passing attack.

Kiffin wants more balance from LSU’s offense

Kiffin’s defense of Leavitt also comes as LSU works through a larger offensive problem. Entering Week 4, the Tigers had completed 65 of 104 passes, with Leavitt throwing five interceptions. Meanwhile, the running game had been much more productive, averaging 209.3 yards per game, 4.4 yards per carry and 10 rushing touchdowns.

Kiffin acknowledged the contrast. LSU supporters had spent much of the offseason asking him to improve the rushing attack, but the Tigers now need greater consistency through the air.

He said LSU must cut down on incompletions and make the passing game complement what has been an effective ground attack.

Leavitt’s season, however, can’t be judged entirely by his showing against Ole Miss. Against Clemson, he completed 16 of 28 passes for 230 yards and a touchdown while rushing for 113 yards and two scores in LSU’s 51-10 victory.

He also threw for 344 yards against Louisiana Tech, although three interceptions hurt his overall performance. His six rushing touchdowns have made his mobility an important part of LSU’s offensive identity.

On the other side, Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss produced a standout performance in Oxford. He threw for 363 yards and two touchdowns before adding the decisive fourth-quarter rushing score. His ability to make timely throws and create plays with his legs helped the Rebels hold off LSU.

The Tigers now turn their attention to Texas A&M, with both teams entering the matchup at 2-1.

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian addresses the challenge of having Donald Trump at Texas games as communication with players gets disrupted
articles.standfirst: President Donald Trump is set to attend the first regular-season matchup between the Longhorns and the Volunteers
articles.summary: President Donald Trump is set to attend the first regular-season matchup between the Longhorns and the Volunteers
articles.body:
This week of college football has all the ingredients to be one of the absolute best in recent memory, highlighted by six AP-ranked matchups on the same day for the first time since 2023 . Headliners feature heavy-hitting battles like No. 1 Texas traveling to face No. 14 Tennessee , No. 4 Ole Miss battling No. 21 Florida , No. 17 Iowa taking on No. 18 Michigan , and No. 23 Texas A&M clashing with No. 10 LSU .

For the top-ranked Texas Longhorns , this Saturday at Neyland Stadium marks their first road test of the campaign and the official opening of a brutal stretch where seven of their final nine games come against teams currently entrenched in the AP Top 25 .

Adding to the massive spectacle, former Volunteers legend Peyton Manning will be in attendance alongside a sold-out crowd of over 100,000 fans , plus a very special guest, as President Donald Trump is scheduled to attend the historic showdown at noon ET.

Notably, it marks only the fourth meeting all-time between the two iconic programs, with their previous three matchups all taking place in the Cotton Bowl (Tennessee winning in 1951, and Texas taking victories in 1953 and 1969).

Steve Sarkisian Highlights Secret Service Protocol and Headset Blackouts

Having high-profile political figures watch a game in person brings unique benefits alongside logistical hurdles, and Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian recently pulled back the curtain on one of the most frustrating side effects regarding Donald Trump's attendance .

Speaking during a media briefing, Sarkisian explained that coach-to-coach and coach-to-player headset communications are cut briefly whenever Trump enters, exits, or moves locations within the stadium, a mandatory security protocol enforced by the Secret Service given the immense crowd of over 100,000 spectators .

"The one thing that you have to be aware of when the president goes to any game is that any time he enters the stadium or leaves the stadium, or changes locations within the stadium, they cut all communication," Sarkisian stated. "You have to have a plan for that if and/or when, and you get no warning. So that just gets cut out."

Sarkisian noted that Miami head coach Mario Cristobal shared a similar experience from the previous season's postseason, warning that when security details forced communication lines to drop during crucial late-game drives, teams received zero advance notice.

While coach-to-coach headsets have been a sideline staple for decades, coach-to-player communication was only officially approved in college football starting in the 2024 season , allowing one offensive and one defensive player per team to receive direct instructions until the play clock ticks down to 15 seconds.

When unexpected security blackouts occur due to movements by Donald Trump or security details, coaching staffs must instantly revert to backup hand signals.

After this game Texas begins a punishing October slate immediately following a well-earned bye week.

The Longhorns face the Red River Rivalry against Oklahoma , followed by a terrifying five-game stretch against currently ranked opponents: home dates against Florida , Ole Miss , and Mississippi State , paired with challenging road trips to Missouri and LSU .

articles.title: Colorado Buffaloes vs Baylor Bears: What time is Deion Sanders’ team playing and where to watch the college football game
articles.standfirst: Baylor Opens as Heavy Favorite Against Colorado in Week 4 Showdown
articles.summary: Baylor Opens as Heavy Favorite Against Colorado in Week 4 Showdown
articles.body:
The 2026 college football season continues with a marquee non-conference clash as the Baylor Bears host the Colorado Buffaloes to open the NCAA Division FBS campaign. It's a headliner for this weekend pitting two ambitious programs against one another, and the betting market has already staked out a clear position on how it expects the afternoon to unfold.

When and where to watch the Colorado Buffaloes vs Baylor Bears game

The game is scheduled for this Saturday, September 26, 2026, with kickoff set for 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time (11:00 a.m. Central time and 9:00 a.m. Pacific Time). This is a Regular Season

matchup, meaning both teams will be showing their opening hand of the year with a full offseason of preparation behind them.

The college football games coverage this season is carried across different networks, but for this particular game between the Colorado Buffaloes and the Baylor Bears, you’ll be able to watch it on ESPN2 and through platforms like Fubo, DIRECTV, Hulu + Live TV, and Sling TV.

What's at stake in the Colorado Buffaloes vs Baylor Bears game?

Because this is a regular season game, non-conference meeting, the immediate implications are less about standings and more about tone-setting. A statement win would validate Baylor's status as the favorite and give the Bears early momentum before conference play heats up.

For Colorado, the equation is simpler and arguably more valuable : a road upset — or even a spread-covering loss that keeps the score respectable — would announce the Buffaloes as a team ready to punch above their preseason billing.

During the first couple of weeks results carry outsized weight in the college football landscape, where a limited regular season means every game shapes the postseason conversation. A tight, high-scoring contest between two Power programs is exactly the kind of resume-shaping opener both coaching staffs will have circled.

Baylor's path is the straightforward one the market is pricing in: protect home turf, control the line of scrimmage, and lean on the crowd advantage to build an early lead. The Bears don't need to reinvent the wheel — they need to convert their favored status into the double-digit margin the spread demands.

Colorado's path hinges on discipline and explosiveness. Underdogs who cover in openers typically do it by winning the turnover battle, hitting a couple of chunk plays, and hanging around long enough to make the fourth quarter tense. At +9.5 to +10.5, the Buffaloes don't have to win outright to reward their backers — they simply have to keep the deficit in single digits.

Prediction for the Colorado Buffaloes vs Baylor Bears

The number tells the story: Baylor is a heavy favorite for a reason, and playing at home in a season opener only sharpens that edge. Expect the Bears to establish control and carry a lead into the second half. But with a total in the mid-50s and a spread hovering around 10, this profiles as a game where Colorado's offense keeps things within range late.

The lean: Baylor to win, but Colorado to cover the spread in a high-scoring opener that flirts with — and could clear — the Over. Call it a Baylor victory by a touchdown, with the total landing right around that 55-point line.

articles.standfirst: Tennessee Volunteers Host Texas Longhorns in a Marquee Season-Opening Clash
articles.summary: Tennessee Volunteers Host Texas Longhorns in a Marquee Season-Opening Clash
articles.body:
The 2026 - 2027 college football season brings a heavyweight collision: the Tennessee Volunteers welcome the Texas Longhorns in a Week 4 matchup that instantly announces itself as one of the most consequential games on the opening slate.

This is the kind of non-conference-caliber showdown that sets the tone for an entire campaign — two proud programs, two national brands, and a national audience tuning in from the very first Saturday.

Texas Longhorns vs Tennessee Volunteers: When and where to watch the game

Mark the date: the Tennessee Volunteers and Texas Longhorns square off on Saturday, September 26, 2026, with kickoff set for 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time (11:00 a.m. Central time and 9:00 a.m. Pacific Time).

The college football games coverage this season is carried across different networks, but for this particular game between the Texas Longhorns vs Tennessee Volunteers, you’ll be able to watch it on ABC and through platforms like ABC YouTube TV.

The Matchup: Volunteers vs Longhorns

Tennessee holds the home-field edge, and in college football that advantage is rarely trivial. An early-season home crowd, energized after a long offseason, can be a genuine twelfth man — swinging momentum, forcing false starts, and turning a close game in the fourth quarter. The Volunteers will want to lean on that atmosphere , establish tempo early, and put the Longhorns on their heels before the visitors settle into a rhythm.

Texas, for its part, arrives as a program accustomed to the spotlight and to hostile road environments. The Longhorns' challenge is the classic road opener: absorb the early surge, weather the crowd noise, and stay composed through the first quarter. Teams that survive that opening barrage on the road often find the environment works in their favor as the game wears on, quieting the home fans and stealing the emotional edge.

The tactical battle will likely come down to a few familiar Week 4 themes. Which offense is further along in its execution? Which defensive front can generate pressure without over-committing against unproven personnel? And crucially, which team wins the turnover margin — the single most reliable predictor of outcomes in games where both sides are still finding their footing.

Early-season football is often decided less by scheme and more by cleanliness: penalties, ball security, and third-down discipline.

What's at stake for the rest of the College Football season?

For both the Volunteers and the Longhorns, this is far more than a season game — it is a measuring stick . A convincing performance here validates an offseason of work and immediately inserts the winner into the national conversation.

Because this game falls in the very first week, its result will echo throughout the season: strength-of-schedule arguments, ranking momentum, and the confidence that carries a locker room through the grind of the fall all trace back to how a program handles a marquee opener like this one.

There is also the intangible element of program prestige. Games between name-brand powers are recruiting theater as much as they are football contests. Every big play, every stop, every roar of the home crowd is being watched by prospects across the country. The winner doesn't just bank a "W" — it banks momentum on the recruiting trail and belief inside its own building.

What is our prediction for the Texas Longhorns vs Tennessee Volunteers game?

This has the makings of a taut, physical opener between two evenly matched programs, and games like this often hinge on the smallest margins — a red-zone stop, a special-teams swing, a single turnover.

Home-field advantage is real, and in a Week 4 environment where crowd energy peaks, the edge tilts slightly toward the Tennessee Volunteers. Expect a competitive, closely contested affair that stays within one possession into the fourth quarter, with the home side's atmosphere proving the difference in a tight finish.

Whatever the outcome, the college football season could hardly ask for a better opening act. Circle Saturday, September 26 — the Volunteers and Longhorns are set to deliver.

articles.title: Social media shreds bizarre national anthem before No. 1 Texas vs. Tennessee SEC clash
articles.standfirst: Pregame ceremony takes unexpected turn as fans mock anthem performance
articles.summary: Pregame ceremony takes unexpected turn as fans mock anthem performance
articles.body:
Social media found an unexpected talking point before the highly anticipated SEC showdown between No. 1 Texas and No. 14 Tennessee, and it arrived before either team had taken a snap.

A pregame rendition of “The Star-Spangled Banner” at Neyland Stadium quickly became the focus of online reactions as viewers questioned the unusual delivery.

ESPN’s College GameDay, which was broadcasting its final hour from inside the stadium, showed the anthem during the buildup to a sold-out afternoon in Knoxville.

The performance was scheduled for 11:59 a.m. ET, immediately followed by a military flyover featuring two F-35 Lightning aircraft and a KC-135 Stratotanker. Tennessee confirmed that the flyover was a joint effort involving the 134th Air Refueling Wing at McGhee Tyson Air National Guard Base and the 33rd Fighter Wing at Eglin Air Force Base.

The elaborate pregame production reflected the scale of the occasion. Texas entered the contest ranked No. 1 nationally, while Tennessee was ranked No. 14 in the AP poll.

The game also marked Texas’ first regular-season appearance at Neyland Stadium, with the Longhorns and Volunteers meeting in the SEC for the first time.

Fans turn anthem into pregame spectacle

Rather than setting the stage for the matchup, the anthem quickly became a social media spectacle of its own. One fan called the Tennessee rendition “the most unserious thing” they’d ever heard, while another viewer posted a blunt question about what had happened during the Knoxville performance.

Another user took aim at the combination of singing and instrumentation, writing, “Gotta sing or play it, can not do both yikes.” A separate reaction labeled it among the worst national anthem performances ever shown on ESPN.

The reactions gained momentum because the anthem appeared during an already dramatic sequence. With more than 100,000 fans packed into Neyland Stadium, the flyover and patriotic ceremony were intended to form part of a major opening spectacle.

Instead, the singer’s interpretation became the moment many viewers were discussing online.

President Donald Trump’s scheduled attendance added another major storyline to the game. His visit prompted enhanced security screening at all stadium gates, along with additional checkpoints around the venue. Tennessee officials urged fans to arrive well ahead of kickoff because of the expected delays.

The presidential visit also created an unusual subplot for the broadcast and teams. Reports noted that Trump’s movements around Neyland Stadium could potentially interfere with communications equipment used by coaches.

That concern later became relevant when audio issues affected the ABC broadcast during the game.

Still, before the football itself took center stage, the anthem had already generated plenty of conversation.

articles.title: Air Force One low pass wows fans before Trump joins SEC clash in Austin
articles.standfirst: Fans get an unexpected aerial display before the president reaches the stadium for kickoff
articles.summary: Fans get an unexpected aerial display before the president reaches the stadium for kickoff
articles.body:
Air Force One turned an already highly anticipated college football afternoon into a memorable spectacle Saturday, soaring at low altitude over Neyland Stadium shortly before President Donald Trump arrived to watch the SEC showdown between No. 1 Texas and No. 14 Tennessee.

The presidential aircraft passed above the Knoxville stadium shortly before 11:30 a.m. ET, giving fans in the stands an unexpected pregame sight as players from both teams warmed up on the field.

Trump landed at McGhee Tyson Airport at 11:28 a.m. before making his way to the stadium by motorcade. He arrived at Neyland Stadium at 11:59 a.m., just before the national anthem and the noon kickoff.

The flyover added another layer of pageantry to a game that already had enormous attention. Texas entered the contest ranked No. 1, while Tennessee was No. 14, with both teams unbeaten heading into the meeting.

The matchup also marked quarterback Arch Manning's first appearance at Neyland Stadium, where his uncle Peyton Manning became one of Tennessee's most celebrated players.

Fans were encouraged to arrive significantly earlier than normal because of the additional security arrangements surrounding the president's visit.

Stadium gates opened at 9 a.m., and early arrivals were offered discounted concessions. The strategy appeared to work, with large numbers of spectators already inside well before kickoff.

The sight of Air Force One passing overhead became an unexpected highlight before the football began for those who'd taken their seats early

Trump's visit creates unusual communications challenge

The presidential appearance wasn't only a spectacle for spectators. Texas coach Steve Sarkisian had warned during the week that Trump's movements inside Neyland Stadium could temporarily affect communication systems used by both teams.

Sarkisian explained that coaches could lose their headsets whenever the president enters the stadium, leaves or moves between locations. That includes communications between coaches and the systems used to relay information to players.

“The one thing that you have to be aware of when the president goes to any game is that any time he enters the stadium or leaves the stadium, or changes locations within the stadium, they cut all communication,” Sarkisian said.

The issue had also become a talking point after January's College Football Playoff championship game involving Indiana and Miami. Indiana coach Curt Cignetti later recalled that his team experienced a brief communication problem when Trump left the game, saying there were two or three plays when the devices couldn't be heard.

However, accounts differed over exactly when the interruption occurred, and the communications issue wasn't established as the reason for the game's result.

Trump's attendance in Knoxville continues his pattern of appearing at major sporting events, bringing heightened security and additional attention wherever he goes.

articles.title: 'Absolute idiotic move': Texas star Colin Simmons flagged for 'simulating using the restroom' after huge sack
articles.standfirst: Simmons dominated Tennessee’s offense but was flagged after an ill-timed celebration following a sack
articles.summary: Simmons dominated Tennessee’s offense but was flagged after an ill-timed celebration following a sack
articles.body:
Colin Simmons delivered a historic defensive performance against Tennessee on Saturday, but one bizarre celebration quickly became one of the most talked-about moments of the game.

The Texas defensive standout was penalized for unsportsmanlike conduct after appearing to imitate urinating on the field following a sack of Tennessee quarterback Faizon Brandon.

The incident occurred during the second quarter at Neyland Stadium, with top-ranked Texas visiting No. 14 Tennessee in a highly anticipated SEC matchup.

Simmons had just brought Brandon down for a 16-yard loss when he performed the gesture. The officials immediately threw a flag, and the referee announced the infraction as “simulating using the restroom.”

The penalty completely changed the value of the defensive play. Instead of leaving Tennessee facing a long-distance situation after losing 16 yards, the Volunteers were awarded 15 yards and an automatic first down.

Tennessee took advantage of the extended possession by moving beyond midfield, although Texas ultimately prevented the drive from producing points. The Longhorns forced an incomplete pass on fourth down and regained possession.

The unusual celebration also caught the attention of the ABC broadcast team. ESPN analyst Kirk Herbstreit strongly criticized the decision, calling it an “absolute idiotic move,” while play-by-play announcer Chris Fowler described the gesture as especially vulgar.

“It’s idiotic, and it doesn’t get much more vulgar, either,” said Fowler .

Despite the costly penalty, Simmons ' afternoon was about far more than one questionable celebration.

Simmons puts together record-setting performance

The Texas star continued to dominate Tennessee's offensive line and finished the contest with five sacks, tying the program's single-game record. His performance helped Texas produce 10 sacks overall and withstand a late Tennessee rally to secure a 20-17 victory.

Simmons already had two sacks before halftime, giving Texas a major advantage against Brandon , who was making his SEC debut. He then added three more sacks during the second half. Interestingly, Simmons didn't celebrate after either of his back-to-back sacks in the third quarter.

Texas needed its defense to remain aggressive because the offense struggled to consistently pull away. Arch Manning finished with 201 passing yards and was sacked six times, while Tennessee eventually erased a 10-3 deficit after Qua Moss returned a punt 57 yards for a touchdown.

The Volunteers then pushed the game into a tense finish. Brandon led an 80-yard touchdown drive that ended with a 30-yard scoring pass to Mike Matthews with only 1:22 remaining. Tennessee recovered the ensuing onside kick, but Texas' defense made the final play, batting away Brandon's pass in the end zone.

The victory moved Texas to 4-0, while Tennessee fell to 3-1. The Longhorns did have plenty to clean up, committing 11 penalties for 115 yards.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith turns a historic four-touchdown performance into a Heisman Trophy statement at Ohio State
articles.standfirst: Smith had one of the best games in Ohio State’s history and a career-high day, scoring four touchdowns
articles.summary: Smith had one of the best games in Ohio State’s history and a career-high day, scoring four touchdowns
articles.body:
While much of the college football world was focused on the high-stakes thriller in Knoxville, where President Donald Trump was present and top-ranked Texas narrowly defeated Tennessee 20-17 , the Ohio State Buckeyes were putting on an offensive masterclass closer to home.

Playing inside Ohio Stadium, the Buckeyes cruised to a dominant 42-19 victory over the Illinois Fighting Illini to open conference play.

While the defense clamped down when it mattered, the afternoon belonged entirely to superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, whose electrifying performance solidified his status as an early frontrunner for the Heisman Trophy and a guaranteed top-tier selection in the 2027 NFL Draft .

Jeremiah Smith Enters Record Books With Career Day

Smith put together a jaw-dropping outing against Illinois, setting career highs across the board with 12 receptions, 217 receiving yards, and four touchdowns .

His four trips to the end zone set a brand-new Ohio State single-game record , elevating him alongside program legend Terry Glenn (1995) as the only players in school history to eclipse 200 receiving yards and four touchdowns in a single contest.

Powered by quarterback Julian Sayin , who completed 27-of-36 passes for 367 yards and five total scores , Smith carved up the Fighting Illini secondary from start to finish.

With this explosive exhibition, Smith pushed his career totals to 196 receptions, 3,175 receiving yards, and 34 touchdown catches , putting him within striking distance of breaking multiple historical milestones in Columbus.

Following this historic outing, Smith sits just two touchdowns away from surpassing Chris Olave’s storied school record of 35 career scoring receptions, while rapidly approaching Emeka Egbuka’s program benchmark of 205 total receptions .

If he maintains this ridiculous pace heading into next week's matchup against Iowa, he will shatter both marks well ahead of schedule.

Unquestionably tracking toward becoming the greatest receiver in Ohio State history, Smith is rewriting the standard for excellence in a program that has famously turned Columbus into the ultimate breeding ground for elite NFL pass-catchers like Michael Thomas , Terry McLaurin , Chris Olave , Garrett Wilson , Jaxon Smith-Njigba , and Emeka Egbuka .

articles.title: Texas Longhorns win unofficial title after close win against Tennessee Volunteers
articles.standfirst: The No. 1 team in the country once again grinded out a marginal victory against a ranked team.
articles.summary: The No. 1 team in the country once again grinded out a marginal victory against a ranked team.
articles.body:
It wasn’t overly pretty or dominant, but the Texas Longhorns once again found a way to take down a Top 25 team in a tightly contested game. Two weeks after beating No. 1 Ohio State , the now No. 1 Longhorns defeated the No. 14 Tennessee Volunteers on the road on Saturday.

The Longhorns defense was outstanding, racking up 10 total sacks . Star EDGE defender Colin Simmons had a career day, notching a whopping five sacks all on his own. Quarterback Arch Manning did enough to move the offense, and Raleek Brown punched in two touchdowns on the ground.

While a Week 4 victory doesn’t necessarily mean a ton in the grand scheme of things, the Longhorns will at least hold on to their No. 1 ranking for at least one more week. In addition, they earned themselves an unofficial title - at least only in the eyes of some fans .

Texas Longhorns now considered “The Real UT” after win over Tennessee Volunteers, according to some

The official Yahoo Sports social media account on X got Volunteers fans riled up following the game, by claiming that Texas “ claims the title of ‘The Real UT’ ”. That obviously didn’t sit well with Tennessee fans and alumni.

“ LOL The f**k they did. ”

“ Wrong! It never has and never will. This horse was beat dead long ago. It doesn't come down to a single win. ”

“ THREE points won the game, but there is ZERO debate regarding which “UT” was FIRST. ”

For Volunteers fans, there’s simply no debate: Texas can never be UT due to their respective histories . Meanwhile, Longhorns fans are feeling entitled to take that crown.

articles.title: “Difficult to find a weakness in Jeremiah Smith’s game”: Draft analyst praises the best WR prospect
articles.standfirst: The Ohio State receiver continues to elevate the conversation around him as his name gains momentum ahead of the 2027 NFL Draft.
articles.summary: The Ohio State receiver continues to elevate the conversation around him as his name gains momentum ahead of the 2027 NFL Draft.
articles.body:
J eremiah Smith is entering a stage of his college career where every performance can shift the conversation about his future. And as scouts take a closer look at what he could bring to the NFL, there is one question that is becoming especially difficult to answer: where is his weakness?

A prospect who doesn't rely on just one strength

Draft analyst Jacob Infante ran into that same problem when evaluating Smith, writing: “genuinely difficult to find a weakness in Jeremiah Smith’s game.”

The reason comes down to the number of tools he brings to the same profile. Smith stands 6'3" and weighs around 225 pounds, but his size is only the starting point .

He can attack deep, find openings when coverage closes in and come down with passes that other receivers simply wouldn't be able to reach. That ability allows him to make catches in places where it initially looked like there was very little room left to make a play.

Against Illinois, Smith put all of it on display

The latest test came on September 26, when Ohio State faced Illinois.

Smith finished the afternoon with 12 receptions for 217 yards and four touchdowns in the Buckeyes' 42-19 win .

The numbers alone show the scale of his performance, but the plays revealed something more interesting about how he got there.

In the first quarter, S mith turned a double move into a 72-yard touchdown , leaving the defender behind before accelerating into the end zone.

His third touchdown showed a completely different skill. He caught the ball in the corner of the end zone with a defender on top of him and completed a toe-tap reception, keeping both feet in bounds.

For his fourth, he won with his movement again. A change of direction left Illinois cornerback Juice Clarke out of position and created enough separation for Smith to complete another touchdown.

Four touchdowns, three different ways of creating an advantage and a performance that set career highs in both receptions and receiving yards.

He also just made Ohio State history

Smith's production against Illinois had another consequence that went beyond the game itself.

With his 217 yards, Smith surpassed 3,000 career receiving yards and became the first player in Ohio State history to reach that mark.

The record matters because it puts his season into a bigger context. Smith isn't just putting together big games; he's building one of the most productive receiving careers the program has seen.

And while that record is now part of Ohio State history, his next step is starting to take shape much farther from Columbus.

Why are the Miami Dolphins part of the conversation?

The Miami Dolphins appear in some 2027 mock draft scenarios with a very high pick , making them one of the teams linked to Smith.

Miami's situation is particularly interesting. After Tua Tagovailoa's departure, the team entered the 2026 season with Malik Willis as its quarterback.

In Infante's mock draft, the Dolphins end up selecting Smith under the assumption that they retain a high draft position . The analyst notes that, in a real scenario, Miami could try to trade the pick, but his exercise does not account for trades, so the team ends up taking the best player available.

The selection also raises an interesting question for the franchise: if Willis manages to convince the team during the 2026 season, Miami could have less reason to use a pick that high on another quarterback and more room to address another position.

That's where Smith becomes an especially intriguing possibility.

Now the pressure is on everything that comes next

Smith still has the rest of the season ahead of him at Ohio State, and his name is also climbing higher in the Heisman Trophy conversation.

His performance against Illinois gave him more ammunition on both fronts , but the bigger question now is what happens over the next few weeks.

The analyst notes that, in a real scenario, Miami could try to trade the pick, but his exercise does not account for trades, so the team ends up taking the best player available.

The selection also raises an interesting question for the franchise: if Willis manages to convince the team during the 2026 season, Miami could have less reason to use a pick that high on another quarterback and more room to address another position.
That's where Smith becomes an especially intriguing possibility.
Now the pressure is on everything that comes next
Smith still has the rest of the season ahead of him at Ohio State, and his name is also climbing higher in the Heisman Trophy conversation.
His performance against Illinois gave him more ammunition on both fronts , but the bigger question now is what happens over the next few weeks.

articles.title: Positive Dante Moore update delivered by Oregon after star QB got hit late by much-maligned USC linebacker
articles.standfirst: Moore got hit while sliding and his head hit the ground extremely hard, forcing him to be stretchered off and taken to a local hospital.
articles.summary: Moore got hit while sliding and his head hit the ground extremely hard, forcing him to be stretchered off and taken to a local hospital.
articles.body:
Saturday night's matchup between the Oregon Ducks and USC Trojans was supposed to be an epic contest for various reasons. The No. 20 and No. 12 teams, respectively, in the nation going toe-to-toe at the Coliseum in Los Angeles set the perfect stage.

It was always going to be a heated game due to their longstanding rivalry, but USC linebacker Desman Stephens let his emotions get the best of him in a very bad way early in the second quarter. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore ran for a first down and began sliding with Stephens just a couple of yards away.

Instead of pulling up, Stephens launched himself into Moore. Stephens' shoulder made contact with Moore's head, which then slammed into the ground and knocked him unconscious . Moore had to be immobilized and taken off on a stretcher. He was then transported to a local hospital.

Dante Moore has movement in all of his extremities

Thankfully, there's already a positive update on Moore's health. An Oregon team spokesperson confirmed before the game concluded that Moore has movement in all of his extremities and is currently being evaluated at the hospital.

Stephens ended up becoming the story of the game, as his behavior following the hit rubbed just about everyone the wrong way. Stephens was seen celebrating and smiling, even though Moore was lying unconscious on the field . It was a terrible look for Stephens, who was ejected from the game for the targeting penalty.

The Ducks ended up rallying without Moore, as Dylan Raiola came on in relief and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns . Oregon won the game 41-27 .

articles.title: Desman Stephens II makes a drastic decision after delivering dirty blow to Dante Moore that sent him to the hospital
articles.standfirst: Stephens II delivered a late hit on the Oregon Ducks quarterback and celebrated afterwards.
articles.summary: Stephens II delivered a late hit on the Oregon Ducks quarterback and celebrated afterwards.
articles.body:
Desman Stephens II has made a drastic move on social media after his targeting hit on the Oregon Ducks ’ Dante Moore sparked a furious reaction during Saturday's game against USC Trojans . The Trojans linebacker was ejected after striking Moore on September 26 as the quarterback attempted to slide during the second quarter, needing medical attention on the field for several minutes.

Moore had escaped the pocket and picked up a first down before beginning his slide, only for Stephens to make contact with his head and upper body as his head then struck the turf, prompting medical personnel to rush onto the field. He was then taken away on a stretcher in a neck brace and transported to a Los Angeles hospital and the collision immediately turned an intense rivalry game into a frightening scene as Oregon 's players reacted angrily, with both teams involved in a confrontation after the play. Stephens was disqualified for targeting, while Moore was eventually placed on a backboard and taken toward a waiting ambulance and the Oregon coach Dan Lanning later provided an encouraging update on his quarterback's condition. “He's in recovery, so I don't want to speak too soon, but he's moving; he has the ability to move," Lanning said. "So, we'll continue to assess him, but I don't want to speak too soon, but he's moving."

Desman Stephens II locks down social media after backlash

Stephens ' actions after the hit also became a major part of the discussion, with video showing the USC player appearing to celebrate with teammates after being removed from the game, and that reaction drew further criticism online. Fans flooded Stephens ' Instagram posts with angry comments. More than 1,800 comments were reportedly left in roughly 20 minutes before his account was switched to private to block people from giving their thoughts to him directly. Some of the online reaction crossed a far more serious line, with reports that users shared images and an alleged address connected to Stephens ' family. Such behavior amounts to harassment and raises obvious concerns beyond normal criticism of an athlete's actions. One user wrote on Instagram, “Don't be a fake demon now. He thought s**t was funny laughing on the sidelines.” A second said, “Can't wait for that chat gpt apology next.” And a third bluntly captured the sentiment by commenting, “Coward.” On the field, Oregon ultimately responded to Moore 's injury by rallying behind backup quarterback Dylan Raiola and securing a 41-27 victory over USC . Raiola completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns, including a 3-yard scoring pass to Evan Stewart shortly after entering the game. He then helped Oregon produce four touchdown drives after halftime.

articles.title: Silver Lining: Oregon’s Dante Moore diagnosed with concussion, avoids long-term injury after scary hit
articles.standfirst: The Ducks quarterback is expected back this season after avoiding any additional damage
articles.summary: The Ducks quarterback is expected back this season after avoiding any additional damage
articles.body:
Oregon ’s 41-27 win over USC should have been defined by a statement road victory. Instead, the lasting image from Saturday night was Dante Moore on the turf after a frightening hit that immediately shifted the focus from the scoreboard to his health.

Moore was injured in the first half after scrambling and sliding, only to be contacted by USC defender Desman Stephens II . His head struck the turf, and the quarterback remained down for nearly 15 minutes before leaving the game.

The initial scene was alarming enough to raise fears of something more serious. By Sunday morning, Oregon had received a much more encouraging update as Moore is dealing with a concussion, but no additional injuries were discovered, and he is expected to return at some point this season.

That doesn't give the Ducks a timetable, and it doesn't mean Moore will be rushed back. It does, however, provide a significant measure of relief after how the injury looked in real time.

Oregon can afford to be cautious with Moore

Moore ’s status carries enormous importance for a Ducks team with championship ambitions. He returned to Oregon this season after turning down the NFL Draft, where he was widely expected to be selected in the top 10.

The decision gave him another opportunity to chase a title in Eugene and strengthen his case to become the No.1 overall pick in 2027. Now, the priority is making sure he is fully healthy before returning.

Oregon ’s upcoming schedule helps. The Ducks are off in Week 5, giving Moore additional recovery time before their next game against UCLA on October 10. That break could prove valuable as he works through concussion protocol.

Dylan Raiola changed outlook immediately

The other reason Oregon doesn't have to panic is what happened after Moore left. Dylan Raiola stepped in and delivered exactly what the Ducks needed.

The Nebraska transfer completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns, helping Oregon pull away in a game that was tied in the fourth quarter.

His performance showed why the Ducks invested in an experienced backup quarterback through the transfer portal. Dierre Hill Jr. and Jordon Davison also helped steady the offense, combining for 238 yards from scrimmage as Oregon adjusted without its starter.

Oregon left Los Angeles with a two-touchdown victory and proof that its offense can still function without Moore in the short term. That is useful, but the more important development came a day later.

After an injury that briefly made everything else feel secondary, Moore avoided any additional damage and is expected to play again this season. That's the silver lining Oregon needed most.

articles.title: USC suspends Desman Stephens II for 'unacceptable' celebration after hit sends Dante Moore to hospital
articles.standfirst: The Trojans linebacker apologized for smiling while Dante Moore received medical attention
articles.summary: The Trojans linebacker apologized for smiling while Dante Moore received medical attention
articles.body:
USC ’s loss to Oregon produced plenty of football questions, but the most urgent issue by Sunday morning had little to do with the final score.

Linebacker Desman Stephens II was suspended for one game after a targeting hit on Oregon quarterback Dante Moore left the Ducks star down on the field for an extended period.

Stephens ’ reaction afterward, smiling and celebrating with teammates while Moore was still receiving medical attention, drew immediate criticism and prompted USC to act.

The suspension means Stephens will miss next weekend’s game against Washington at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Moore was hurt in the second quarter of Oregon’s 41-27 win when he slid at the end of a scramble and Stephens made contact with his forearm.

Moore ’s head struck the turf, and he remained down for nearly 15 minutes before being taken to a hospital. Stephens was ejected for targeting.

Response did not represent USC

The post-play reaction quickly became the bigger issue for the Trojans .

“Desman’s actions in last night’s game are unacceptable and are not reflective of USC football nor of his personal character,” coach Lincoln Riley said in a statement.

“He understands his mistake, accepts the consequences of his actions and will learn from this. The entire Trojan Family wishes Dante a full recovery, and we send our best regards to him and his family.”

USC ’s decision came less than a day after the game, signaling how seriously the program viewed what happened after the hit.

Stephens also released a statement acknowledging that his reaction was indefensible.

“Seeing a player injured like that is incredibly serious, and my reaction in the moments afterward was completely inappropriate and inexcusable,” he said.

“Regardless of what was going through my mind at the time, there is no justification for smiling or celebrating while another player receives medical attention.”

“I take full responsibility for my actions. That is not the person or teammate I want to be, and I will learn from this. I am deeply sorry to Dante, his family and everyone who saw my reaction.

“It is not representative of USC or our program. I hope he makes a full and speedy recovery.”

Moore’s condition remains bigger concern

Oregon coach Dan Lanning said after the game that Moore had regained some movement before being transported to the hospital.

That was the first encouraging sign after a frightening scene that briefly stopped the game and overshadowed much of Oregon ’s victory.

The Trojans will now move forward without Stephens against Washington , but the larger concern remains Moore’s health. USC has already made its judgment on the conduct. Stephens ’ own apology makes clear he understands why.

articles.title: Minnesota’s P.J. Fleck stuns fans by wiping bloody lip of Gophers linebacker onto his own cheek
articles.standfirst: Maverick Baranowski embraced the moment after Fleck smeared blood across his face
articles.summary: Maverick Baranowski embraced the moment after Fleck smeared blood across his face
articles.body:
P.J. Fleck has built his reputation on relentless energy, but even by his standards, Minnesota ’s postgame scene at Washington was extraordinary.

Moments after the Golden Gophers secured a 27-24 road win, Fleck found linebacker Maverick Baranowski bleeding from the mouth after taking a cleat to the face on the final play.

He grabbed Baranowski by the head, pulled him in close and then wiped some of the blood across his own cheeks. “Blood brother,” Fleck said afterward.

The image immediately became one of the strangest visuals of the college football weekend, but to Baranowski , it was completely in character.

“He’s a crazy man,” Baranowski said. “It’s a great moment.”

Celebration reflected deeper relationship

Baranowski has spent all five years of his college career at Minnesota under Fleck , and his postgame comments made clear that their relationship extends beyond the field.

“Winning’s hard in the Big Ten, and when you get to win at a place like this, just so exciting and get to enjoy that with all my teammates and my head coach always having my back for the last five years,” he said.

“I love that guy more than anyone and an awesome opportunity to share that moment with him.”

Fleck later joked about the blood on his face and shirt. “Back in the day, I’m sure that’s what they did, the frontiersmen out West,” he said. “Little blood on there, I guess.”

Receiver Javon Tracy was less convinced he would ever join in. “I would never do that, but P.J., he’s different, man,” Tracy said. “Like, he’s crazy. He’s very energetic.”

Postgame celebration kept getting wilder

The blood-smearing moment was only the beginning. Fleck raced around the field hugging players and staff members, shouted toward the Minnesota fan section and then carried the same energy into the locker room.

There, his players lifted him into the air and crowd-surfed him near the ceiling while chanting, “Coach, coach, coach.” Fleck eventually arrived at his news conference still marked by the celebration and turned the attention back toward Baranowski’s performance.

“The kid loves the game, plays the game the right way,” Fleck said. “He is the heartbeat of our defense and our team.”

Baranowski backed that up with seven tackles, a sack and an interception.

Emotion came after statement Big Ten win

Minnesota improved to 3-1 with the victory, and the road result gave Fleck one of his most memorable celebrations in years.

The coach’s personality often draws attention, but Baranowski has previously described him as much more than an emotional sideline presence.

“I had a conversation with him a couple months ago about some personal stuff, and we talked for hours,” Baranowski said. “It had nothing to do with football. There’s not many people like that in this sport.”

That context helps explain why the postgame scene resonated inside the program. From the outside, it looked outrageous.

To Fleck and Baranowski , it was a moment of trust, adrenaline and a relationship built over five years.

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian blames 'look at me' society for bizarre Colin Simmons urination celebration
articles.standfirst: The Texas coach praised Simmons’ five-sack night but warned that the Longhorns cannot afford repeat mistakes
articles.summary: The Texas coach praised Simmons’ five-sack night but warned that the Longhorns cannot afford repeat mistakes
articles.body:
Texas left Knoxville 4-0 and still looking every bit like a national title contender, but Steve Sarkisian wasn't interested in pretending the night had been flawless.

The Longhorns beat Tennessee 20-17 behind a dominant defensive performance, yet one of the most talked-about moments came after Colin Simmons recorded a sack and then simulated urinating on the field.

Officials flagged him for unsportsmanlike conduct, wiping out the stop and extending Tennessee’s drive. Sarkisian responded immediately.

“We took him out, we addressed it and put him back in,” he said. “At that point, I’m not going to give the guy a death penalty over an unsportsmanlike conduct. We got to fix it though. That can’t continue.”

It was a measured response to a player who had otherwise produced one of the best defensive performances in school history.

Problem is bigger than one celebration

Simmons wasn't the only Texas player whose post-play behavior drew attention. Running back Raleek Brown also produced a provocative celebration after a touchdown, though he wasn't penalized. Sarkisian used both moments to make a wider point.

“Unfortunately, in our society right now, we live in a ‘look at me’ society,” Sarkisian said. “That’s the world that we live in.”

His concern was less about one viral clip and more about keeping the team’s focus where he believes it belongs.

“So we’ve got to get to, it’s about the team and focus on the team, and not so much ‘look at me,’” Sarkisian added. “So we’ll try to improve upon that.”

That matters even more for a team with championship expectations, where a needless 15-yard penalty in the wrong moment could have much greater consequences later in the season.

Simmons mistake came during a historic night

The celebration became the viral moment, but Simmons ’ actual performance was exceptional.

He finished with five sacks, tying a Texas program record, while the Longhorns piled up 10 sacks as a team against Tennessee. Simmons later acknowledged that he went too far.

“I also do want to say I apologize for the celebration,” he said. “I was definitely in that mode feeling myself. But it happens.”

Sarkisian was willing to hold both truths at once. The penalty was unacceptable. The performance was still outstanding.

The Longhorns have already beaten Ohio State and Tennessee , giving them the kind of early résumé that puts every detail under the microscope.

Sarkisian wasn't interested in humiliating Simmons or pretending the mistake erased everything else he did. He was interested in making sure it does not happen again.

Texas has enough talent to contend for a championship. What Sarkisian wants now is the discipline to match it.

articles.summary: Deion “Coach Prime” Sanders is beginning to face the kind of pressure that accompanies unmet expectations in major college football after his Colorado Buffaloes lost to Baylor 23-13. Amidst the drama, a resurfaced video shows Sanders in a heated argument with ESPN reporter Ed Werder during a fiery postgame press conference on September 2, 2023. Coach Prime constantly yells. “"Do you believe now?" to the reporter, who was critical of Deion’s performances with the Buffaloes three years ago. It’s a clear sign that the NFL Hall of Famer needs to find a way to turn things around, and fast.

articles.title: Is Deion "Coach Prime" Sanders’ seat heating up? Colorado’s Baylor loss raises new questions
articles.standfirst: Every college football coach is judged by results, and that's where the legendary player is struggling
articles.summary: Every college football coach is judged by results, and that's where the legendary player is struggling
articles.body:
The most important question surrounding Colorado football after Saturday’s 23-13 loss to Baylor is whether Deion "Coach Prime" Sanders is beginning to face the kind of pressure that accompanies unmet expectations in major college football.

The short answer is no, not yet. But the longer answer is far more complicated after Colorado opened conference play with a frustrating defeat that dropped the Buffaloes to 2-2 overall and 0-1 in the Big 12. For much of Sanders’ tenure in Boulder, wins and losses have only told part of the story.

His arrival transformed Colorado from a national afterthought into one of the sport’s biggest attractions. Television ratings surged, recruiting improved, and the program became one of the most talked-about brands in college athletics. Eventually, however, every college football coach is judged by the same metric: results.

Loss to Baylor highlighted concerns

The Buffaloes actually outgained the Bears 363-337. They threw for 280 yards. Wide receiver Joseph Williams delivered one of the best performances of his career, catching 11 passes for 127 yards. Quanell Farrakhan Jr. added seven receptions for 117 yards and was part of several explosive plays that kept Colorado within striking distance.

On paper, those numbers suggest an offense capable of moving the football. The problem was finishing drives. Colorado converted just three of 15 third-down opportunities and failed on both fourth-down attempts. Repeated chances to sustain momentum disappeared, allowing Baylor to remain in control despite being outgained.

"You’re not going to win like that," Sanders said after the game. "You’re not going to win like that whatsoever." The most significant development came at quarterback. Former five-star recruit Julian Lewis struggled through another uneven performance and was eventually replaced by Isaac Wilson. The move injected life into the offense. Wilson helped erase a 13-3 deficit and guided Colorado to a 13-13 tie early in the fourth quarter.

For a brief moment, it appeared Colorado might escape with a comeback victory. Instead, Baylor responded with 10 unanswered points in the final minutes to secure the win and hand the Buffaloes a disappointing start to conference play.

One of the defining moments of Colorado's season

Lewis arrived in Boulder carrying enormous expectations. Five-star quarterbacks are often viewed as program-changing players, and Sanders invested heavily in the future by placing his trust in the highly touted freshman. Benching him, even temporarily, suggests Colorado's coaching staff believes immediate performance has become more important than long-term development.

That is not necessarily a sign of panic. It is, however, evidence that Sanders recognizes the urgency surrounding this season. The reality is that Deion's job security remains stronger than a typical coach sitting at 2-2. His impact on the university extends far beyond the scoreboard.

Colorado has benefited from unprecedented national exposure, increased revenue opportunities, improved recruiting visibility, and sustained relevance in a crowded college football landscape. Those factors matter to athletic departments. At the same time, the expectations surrounding Sanders have evolved.

Early in his tenure, simply making Colorado competitive again was considered a success. Now the conversation has shifted toward conference contention and postseason appearances. That change is the clearest sign of progress under Sanders, but it also raises the standard by which he will be evaluated.

Pressure for the remainder of the season

The Baylor loss exposed a team still searching for consistency. Colorado showed enough offensive firepower to move the ball between the 20-yard lines, yet lacked the efficiency needed to capitalize on opportunities. The defense largely kept the game within reach before wearing down late. And the quarterback situation, once viewed as settled, suddenly appears uncertain.

None of those issues alone place Sanders on the hot seat. Combined, they create pressure for the remainder of the season. The upcoming home matchup against Texas Tech now carries added significance. Falling to 2-3 and 0-2 in conference play would intensify scrutiny around a program that entered the year with aspirations of competing near the top of the Big 12 standings.

A victory, meanwhile, would ease concerns and restore momentum heading into the heart of league play. That is why Sanders' tenure is not truly on the line right now. What is on the line is the narrative surrounding his program.

For the first time in a while, the conversation is shifting away from Colorado's celebrity appeal and toward its on-field performance. Sanders has spent much of his coaching career proving doubters wrong, and he still has ample time to do so this season.

articles.title: Texas running back Raleek Brown pulls off jaw-dropping 360 spin hurdle vs. Tennessee
articles.summary: Texas running back Raleek Brown gave college football fans one of the most memorable highlights of the weekend during the Longhorns' 20-17 victory over Tennessee. The senior transfer showcased his elite athleticism on a dazzling run that featured a spin move, a full 360-degree turn, and a hurdle over a would-be Volunteer tackler, leaving viewers scrambling to watch the replay again and again. Many viewers immediately drew comparisons to Philadelphia Eagles star Saquon Barkley, whose gravity-defying hurdle became one of the NFL's defining highlights in recent years. While Brown's move had its own flair, the combination of a spin and leap over a defender sparked memories of Barkley's ability to turn routine plays into viral moments.
