articles.title: Why Texas looks like a legitimate title favorite after beating Tennessee on the road
articles.standfirst: The Longhorns have shown that they can win a high-pressure road game against a ranked SEC opponent
articles.summary: The Longhorns have shown that they can win a high-pressure road game against a ranked SEC opponent
articles.body:
Whether the Texas Longhorns ultimately wins the national championship remains to be seen. The SEC schedule is unforgiving, the College Football Playoff field will be loaded, and plenty can change over the next two months.

But the No. 1 Longhorns provided another strong argument that they have the talent and balance to contend for their first national title since 2005. Their latest evidence came in Knoxville, where Texas opened SEC play by winning its first-ever game at Neyland Stadium largely on the strength of a defense that overwhelmed Tennessee. The game ended 20-17.

The Longhorns recorded 10 sacks, the second-highest total in school history, and held the Volunteers to 221 yards of total offense. Tennessee managed just 88 yards in the first half and repeatedly struggled to handle Texas' pass rush. At the center of it was Colin Simmons.

The junior edge rusher tied a program record with five sacks, matching Shane Dronett's 1981 performance against Texas Tech. Simmons also became the first FBS player since 2006 to record five sacks against a ranked opponent.

The damage wasn't limited to Simmons

Rasheem Biles, Alex January, Hero Kanu, Zina Umeozulu and Maraad Watson each added a sack as Texas consistently collapsed the pocket. The Longhorns pressured Tennessee quarterbacks Faizon Brandon and George MacIntyre on 21 of their 50 dropbacks, limiting them to just 2-of-8 passing for seven yards when under pressure.

That performance also took some pressure off Arch Manning. The Texas quarterback completed 14 of 19 passes for 201 yards after opening 6-for-6 for 120 yards. He orchestrated a seven-play, 75-yard touchdown drive on the opening possession, including a 43-yard completion to Emmett Mosley V that set up Raleek Brown's first touchdown.

Brown finished with 67 rushing yards and two touchdowns, including a 4-yard score that pushed Texas' lead to 20-10 in the fourth quarter. The Longhorns were far from flawless offensively, but they were efficient where it mattered. Texas went 3-for-3 in the red zone, scoring two touchdowns and a field goal, while Gianni Spetic remained perfect on the season with seven made kicks.

That balance is what makes Saturday's victory significant

Texas didn't need Manning to throw for 350 yards. It didn't need a 200-yard rushing performance. It needed its defense to take control, its offense to capitalize on opportunities and its special teams to deliver when called upon. All three units did enough.

The victory also continued a broader trend. Texas has won 19 of its last 22 conference games and has collected 16 Top 25 victories since 2023, the most among FBS programs during that span. Still, the biggest test is maintaining that standard.

The Longhorns have only played four games, and the SEC will provide plenty of opportunities to expose weaknesses. Oklahoma awaits in the Red River Rivalry on Oct. 10, followed by the remainder of a conference schedule in which every week can alter the national championship conversation.

For now, though, Texas has already demonstrated something valuable: it can win a high-pressure road game against a ranked SEC opponent without needing a heroic performance from its quarterback. If the Longhorns can sustain that defensive dominance while Manning and the offense continue to develop , they will have a legitimate path to the championship.

articles.title: Former Deion Sanders star player could be the solution to Cam Ward’s nightmare with the Titans
articles.standfirst: The LSU tackle as a player with "elite-level potential in the passing game"
articles.summary: The LSU tackle as a player with "elite-level potential in the passing game"
articles.body:
T he Tennessee Titans could be preparing for a major change at offensive tackle, and one of the most highly regarded linemen in the 2027 NFL Draft could be the player waiting to take over. In his latest 2027 NFL Mock Draft for CBS Sports, NFL Draft analyst Mike Renner projected LSU offensive tackle Jordan Seaton to the Titans with the No. 3 overall pick.

Renner's projection would give Tennessee a potential long-term answer at a premium position while also opening the door for the franchise to move on from veteran tackle Dan Moore Jr. "The Titans can finally get out from under the ugly Dan Moore Jr. contract next offseason and they'll fill his shoes with the most polished pass protector in the class," Renner wrote.

He also highlighted Seaton's athleticism, describing the LSU tackle as a player with "elite-level potential in the passing game" and one of the most impressive athletes at the position. For a Titans team building around quarterback Cam Ward, protecting the passer could become one of the franchise's biggest priorities. Adding a tackle capable of handling elite edge rushers would give Tennessee another foundational piece for its offense.

Seaton's rise to the top of the 2027 draft conversation has taken him through two major college programs. A former five-star recruit from I MG Academy, Seaton originally committed to Colorado , where he played under Pro Football Hall of Famer and then-head coach Deion Sanders.

Seaton immediately established himself as an important piece of the Buffaloes' offensive line. According to LSU, he started 22 games during his two seasons at Colorado, with all of his collegiate snaps coming at left tackle.

His 2025 season further elevated his draft stock. Seaton earned second-team All-Big 12 honors after starting the first nine games of the season before an injury ended his campaign. He played 561 offensive snaps and surrendered only one sack.

That performance helped make him one of the most coveted players in the transfer portal. Seaton ultimately transferred to LSU, joining the Tigers as the No. 1 offensive tackle in the portal. LSU lists him at 6-foot-5 and 311 pounds entering the 2026 season. The Tigers represent another major stage for Seaton, this time against SEC competition and with NFL scouts watching closely.

Why Seaton makes sense for Tennessee

Renner's projection is particularly notable because of the position he is filling in Tennessee. The Titans don't need to manufacture a reason to prioritize offensive tackle. Their quarterback investment makes keeping the pocket clean an essential part of the team's long-term plan, and a potential top-three pick would represent a significant commitment to protecting Ward.

Seaton's athletic profile is a major part of the appeal. Pass protection requires more than size. Tackles have to mirror speed rushers, recover when beaten initially and maintain their balance in space. Renner believes Seaton already possesses the athletic traits to excel in that area, calling his potential in the passing game "elite-level."

That assessment puts significant expectations on Seaton entering his LSU season. The Titans would also have to determine whether replacing Moore i s financially and competitively preferable to retaining him. Renner's mock assumes Tennessee will be in position to move on from Moore next offseason , creating an opening at tackle that Seaton could potentially fill

It's important to remember that a mock draft is a projection, not an indication of Tennessee's actual plans. The Titans have an entire NFL season ahead of them, while Jordan still has an entire college season to complete before his draft stock ultimately takes shape. Still, the projection illustrates how quickly Seaton has become part of the conversation surrounding the top of the 2027 NFL Draft.

articles.title: The crazy story of a college football fan who searches for only the worst seats in every stadium
articles.standfirst: Michael Barker spends thousands each season testing obstructed views and warning fans before they buy
articles.summary: Michael Barker spends thousands each season testing obstructed views and warning fans before they buy
articles.body:
M ichael Barker ’s obsession with college football changed the moment he realized he had paid hundreds of dollars for a seat that barely let him see one of the biggest moments of the game.

In 2018, Barker bought a $250 ticket to watch Washington State face Oregon , a bargain compared with average prices that had climbed above $700. Once he reached his seat, however, he discovered a giant light pole blocking part of the field.

The obstruction hadn't been disclosed, and it eventually cost him a clear view of a six-yard Washington State touchdown. Barker could only tell what had happened by watching the fans around him throw their arms into the air.

“After that, I wanted to warn people about obstructed views because of how I was impacted,” Barker told ESPN. That frustration became the foundation for an unusual mission.

Barker searches for seats fans should avoid

The California real estate agent has since visited 222 college football venues, including all 134 FBS stadiums, while using social media to document sections where architecture, press boxes or support structures can ruin the experience.

His preparation can begin months before a game. Barker studies photos and seating charts, returns to venues when necessary and identifies areas where a press box or stadium structure may interfere with the view.

At Indiana’s Memorial Stadium , he estimated one seat allowed him to see only 64% of the field. At Ohio Stadium , the problem was even worse, with one seat offering a view of only one end zone, roughly 8% of the playing surface.

“You don't know what happens until you put your butt in the seat and you look and can't see the field,” Barker said. “I felt bad for them, but if I can help in any way, then it's worth it.”

His work has also highlighted cases where fans say the obstruction was not clearly disclosed before purchase, including two supporters he encountered at the 2023 Cotton Bowl who could see only around 30% of the field.

The mission comes with heavy travel cost

Barker ’s schedule is as demanding as the stadium research itself. During college football season, he travels to four to six games per week and sometimes attends two or three in the same day. He estimates the entire operation costs about $35,000 per season.

To make that possible, he cuts expenses aggressively. Hotels are often replaced by rental cars or airport floors, while food is bought from grocery stores instead of inside stadiums or terminals.

“I joke that whatever rental car I get, I put the word hotel in front of me. So Hotel Camry, Hotel Jeep,” Barker said.

His online following has also become an important part of the project, with supporters sometimes helping him find tickets or navigate new campuses.

“I would not be traveling if it wasn't for social media,” Barker said. “People are awesome... I have friends all over the country, and it's all because of Twitter and college football.”

Barker has already completed the full FBS stadium circuit, yet he has no plans to walk away from the mission.

“I want to keep doing this as long as I can,” he said. What began with one badly positioned light pole has turned into something much bigger: a nationwide effort to make sure the next fan knows exactly what they are paying to see.

articles.title: Jelani Newman cause of death: Former college football player dies at 25
articles.standfirst: The former Saguaro High School standout and Arizona state champion was remembered for his football career and close ties to his family
articles.summary: The former Saguaro High School standout and Arizona state champion was remembered for his football career and close ties to his family
articles.body:
Former San Jose State offensive lineman Jelani Newman has died at 25 following a motorcycle crash, leaving his family, former teammates and coaches mourning a young man remembered for his football ability, kindness and strong personality.

Reports state that Newman was killed in a motorcycle accident on September 12, although some accounts have differed over the timing of the incident.

Details about where the crash occurred and what led to it haven't been publicly disclosed. No detailed police account has been released, meaning the circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear.

Newman's death was reported by multiple outlets, including the San Francisco Chronicle. San Jose State's football program also paid tribute to its former player, sharing an image of Newman wearing his No. 72 jersey and offering condolences to his family.

The Arizona native had built an impressive football résumé before reaching the college level. At Saguaro High School in Scottsdale, Newman became an important part of one of the state's successful programs.

Newman remembered for football and family

Newman was a two-time Arizona Interscholastic Association first-team All-Region 4A selection and earned first-team All-State honors as a senior in 2018.

That season, Saguaro finished 13-1 and captured the 4A state championship, with Newman playing a significant role along the offensive line.

His performances earned him an opportunity with San Jose State, where he signed in December 2018. Newman redshirted during his first college season before making his college debut in the 2020 Arizona Bowl.

He later appeared in all 12 games during the 2021 season and continued his football career with the Spartans through 2022.

Former Saguaro offensive line coach Mark Martinez remained close to Newman after his high school career. Martinez described him as a son and recalled spending time with him away from football, including family outings and fishing trips.

He also remembered Newman as someone who was deeply connected to the people around him.

Newman's grandmother, Nancy McGee Newman , shared a tribute describing the devastating impact his death has had on the family.

She explained that football had been part of Jelani's life from youth leagues through college and that his No. 72 jersey carried special meaning because it represented his sister and his birth month.

She also said Newman had plans to join the U.S. Army, following in the footsteps of his grandfather, and described his smile and laughter as unforgettable.

Following his death, Newman's friend Domenica Civitano created a GoFundMe campaign to help the family cover funeral and burial expenses.

The fundraiser has a $13,000 goal and was established as loved ones deal with the sudden financial responsibilities that accompany an unexpected death.

Funeral arrangements remain pending as family, friends, former teammates and members of the football community continue to remember Newman and the impact he made during his 25 years.

Reports state that Newman was killed in a motorcycle accident on September 12, although some accounts have differed over the timing of the incident.

Details about where the crash occurred and what led to it haven't been publicly disclosed. No detailed police account has been released, meaning the circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear.

Newman's death was reported by multiple outlets, including the San Francisco Chronicle. San Jose State's football program also paid tribute to its former player, sharing an image of Newman wearing his No. 72 jersey and offering condolences to his family.

The Arizona native had built an impressive football résumé before reaching the college level. At Saguaro High School in Scottsdale, Newman became an important part of one of the state's successful programs.
Newman remembered for football and family
Newman was a two-time Arizona Interscholastic Association first-team All-Region 4A selection and earned first-team All-State honors as a senior in 2018.
That season, Saguaro finished 13-1 and captured the 4A state championship, with Newman playing a significant role along the offensive line.

His performances earned him an opportunity with San Jose State, where he signed in December 2018. Newman redshirted during his first college season before making his college debut in the 2020 Arizona Bowl.
He later appeared in all 12 games during the 2021 season and continued his football career with the Spartans through 2022.

Former Saguaro offensive line coach Mark Martinez remained close to Newman after his high school career. Martinez described him as a son and recalled spending time with him away from football, including family outings and fishing trips.
He also remembered Newman as someone who was deeply connected to the people around him.
Newman's grandmother, Nancy McGee Newman , shared a tribute describing the devastating impact his death has had on the family.
She explained that football had been part of Jelani's life from youth leagues through college and that his No. 72 jersey carried special meaning because it represented his sister and his birth month.
She also said Newman had plans to join the U.S. Army, following in the footsteps of his grandfather, and described his smile and laughter as unforgettable.
Following his death, Newman's friend Domenica Civitano created a GoFundMe campaign to help the family cover funeral and burial expenses.
The fundraiser has a $13,000 goal and was established as loved ones deal with the sudden financial responsibilities that accompany an unexpected death.
Funeral arrangements remain pending as family, friends, former teammates and members of the football community continue to remember Newman and the impact he made during his 25 years.

articles.title: Nation’s longest high school football winning streak ends after historic run
articles.standfirst: A late interception and touchdown seal a dramatic victory for the Massapequa Chiefs
articles.summary: A late interception and touchdown seal a dramatic victory for the Massapequa Chiefs
articles.body:
A remarkable seven-year run ended Monday night on Long Island when Massapequa defeated Garden City 21-14 at Hofstra University, bringing the nation’s longest active high school football winning streak to a dramatic close.

Garden City had won 68 consecutive games, dating back to a November 2019 loss to Lindenhurst. The Trojans also entered the matchup with five straight Long Island championships and 10 consecutive Nassau County titles, making the showdown one of the most anticipated games in the region in years.

The game, originally scheduled for Saturday, was postponed because of a nor’easter. The extra wait only intensified the anticipation before nearly 6,000 fans watched the two unbeaten teams finally meet at Shuart Stadium.

Massapequa, which had won 25 straight entering the contest, struck first through quarterback Luke Garguilo . Garden City answered in the second half, and the game remained tied 14-14 with less than six minutes remaining.

A finish decided by two crucial plays

With Garden City threatening late, Massapequa defensive lineman and captain Ryan Chabus intercepted a screen pass with 1:50 remaining and returned it 20 yards to the Trojans’ 18-yard line. The turnover gave the Chiefs an opportunity to produce the decisive score.

Just 80 seconds later, Massapequa quarterback Luke Garguilo found senior receiver Dylan Milio for a 29-yard touchdown. Milio broke free down the seam and reached the end zone with 30 seconds remaining, putting the Chiefs ahead 21-14.

Garden City couldn’t respond, as Massapequa’s defense forced three incompletions on the final possession. The victory sent the Chiefs’ winning streak to 26 games, now the longest active run in New York state.

The interception was the kind of moment Chabus had expected would decide a matchup between two dominant teams.

“Give extended credit to them — they came out to play,” Chabus told The New York Post. “I knew I had to make a play. That's what football players do. That's what three-time Long Island champions do.”

Milio , meanwhile, described the winning touchdown as a moment that made the long-awaited contest even more meaningful. The senior receiver said the players had been eagerly anticipating the clash and were barely able to focus on school before kickoff.

The matchup was particularly significant because the two programs had never previously met. They competed in different conferences and classifications, but a rule change finally created an opportunity for the Long Island powerhouses to face each other.

Garden City’s defeat ends one of the most impressive winning runs in recent high school football. The Trojans had remained unbeaten since 2019 while collecting five consecutive Long Island championships during the streak.

Massapequa, meanwhile, has built an impressive run of its own. The Chiefs entered the game as three-time defending Long Island champions and now have 26 consecutive victories. Their immediate focus will turn toward continuing that streak and pursuing another championship.

Although Garden City’s national-leading run is over, its place in the sport’s recent history remains significant. The team’s 68-game unbeaten stretch ranks among the most remarkable sustained runs by a high school football program.

The national record, however, remains considerably higher. California’s De La Salle won 151 consecutive games between 1992 and 2004, establishing a benchmark that still stands as the recognized national record.

Monday’s thriller has now added another memorable chapter to Long Island football history, with Massapequa emerging from a battle between two unbeaten powers after a dramatic final minute.

articles.title: Dante Moore injury: Desman Stephens II’s disturbing actions cast a shadow over his apology
articles.standfirst: A one-game suspension leaves unresolved questions about his conduct while Moore’s recovery remains uncertain
articles.summary: A one-game suspension leaves unresolved questions about his conduct while Moore’s recovery remains uncertain
articles.body:
Dante Moore was receiving medical attention on the field. Desman Stephens II, whose hit had injured him, was celebrating . Whatever the USC linebacker understood about Moore’s condition at that moment, an opponent remained down and needed help. That should have been reason enough to stop.

What followed made the incident harder to dismiss as one impulsive reaction . Stephens appeared to celebrate shortly after the hit and exchanged greetings with teammates while medical personnel attended to Moore. He later remained on the sideline cheering for USC. That sequence became part of the controversy alongside the tackle itself.

His apology acknowledged the behavior. It did not explain it

Stephens subsequently accepted responsibility in a statement released by USC. He described his reaction as inappropriate and inexcusable, apologized to Moore and his family, and acknowledged there was no justification for celebrating while another player received treatment. Those words matter, but they leave a difficult question: why did the concern expressed afterward fail to appear in his public behavior during the emergency?

We cannot establish whether his apology came from genuine remorse, public pressure or both. Nor can the absence of a publicly reported visit or personal conversation prove that he has made no private contact. What can be assessed is the contrast between his visible conduct and his later acknowledgment that it was unacceptable. The statement begins the process of accountability; his actions from here will give it credibility.

USC suspended Stephens for its October 3 game against Washington. Moore’s recovery has no confirmed endpoint. Oregon announced that he suffered a concussion, with MRI and CT scans showing no additional injuries. Moore has expressed hope that he will return soon, but that is not medical clearance or a confirmed playing date.

What do NCAA targeting rules say about hits like the one on Dante Moore?

The NCAA’s targeting rules prohibit forcible contact to the head or neck of a defenseless opponent and contact with the crown of the helmet. A confirmed targeting foul carries a 15-yard penalty and disqualification. Stephens was ejected after striking Moore as the Oregon quarterback slid during the second quarter.

The suspension rules changed this year. On March 19, the NCAA’s FBS Oversight Committee approved a trial for the 2026 season that allows a player to participate in the next game after his first targeting disqualification. A second offense requires him to miss the first half of the following game; a third requires a full-game suspension.

That change does not explain Stephens’ entire punishment. The previous automatic carryover suspension applied to second-half targeting fouls, and his hit occurred before halftime. USC imposed the additional one-game ban. Conferences can also review conduct beyond the on-field penalty: the Big Ten’s published sportsmanship policy identifies disrespectful behavior and resulting injury as relevant to disciplinary decisions.

How many games Moore will miss remains unknown. Oregon has a bye before facing UCLA on October 10, so it is not yet established that his absence will exceed Stephens’ suspension. NCAA concussion requirements demand medical clearance before a diagnosed athlete returns to athletic activity. His recovery must follow that assessment, regardless of the schedule.

Previous cases show why counting games cannot predict recovery. Pittsburgh quarterback Mason Rudolph missed the next game after his 2019 concussion and later cleared the protocol. Miami’s Tua Tagovailoa missed four games after his September 2024 concussion, with injured reserve requiring that minimum absence. Their circumstances differed, and neither provides a timetable for Moore.

Former NFL quarterback Chase Daniel condemned the hit and emphasized that Moore was giving himself up.

The case still warrants a harder discussion about punishment and empathy. A suspension need not match an injured player’s recovery, but its length should come with a clear explanation of how the hit, the harm and the conduct afterward were weighed . Stephens has acknowledged that his celebration was inexcusable. Demonstrating concern for the person who was hurt is now the responsibility that extends beyond serving one game.

articles.title: Colin Simmons faces calls for suspension after controversial "pee" celebration
articles.standfirst: Texas star Colin Simmons sparks controversy after controversial celebration leads to calls for punishment
articles.summary: Texas star Colin Simmons sparks controversy after controversial celebration leads to calls for punishment
articles.body:
The Texas Longhorns program secured another statement victory on Saturday afternoon by defeating the Tennessee Volunteers on the road, but the win was overshadowed by the controversial celebration from pass rusher Colin Simmons .

After recording a sack, the defensive standout made a gesture simulating urination, an action that resulted in an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty and sparked a wave of criticism across the college football world.

The controversy grew when Houston Chronicle columnist Kirk Bohls argued that both Simmons and teammate Raleek Brown , who also took part in the celebration, should face disciplinary action from the program.

“Texas should fine both players for their lewd actions on a nationally televised platform in front of 101,915 fans, including President Donald Trump, and millions more watching. It should be obvious by now that these college players are indeed professionals because they are paid handsomely to play football and are representing the school,” Bohls wrote.

Although Bohls referenced President Trump’s presence at the stadium as part of his argument, the controversy extended beyond that detail. Several voices within college football criticized the celebration and called for consequences for the players.

Despite the backlash, Simmons and Brown moved past the controversy with their performances on the field. Both defenders delivered strong outings against Tennessee and played key roles in helping the Longhorns secure a narrow victory, keeping their perfect start alive with a 4-0 record in the 2026 season .

Texas remains the No. 1 team in the national rankings and will have a bye week before returning to action on October 10 , when they face the Oklahoma Sooners in another edition of the Red River Rivalry .

articles.title: Arch Manning draft debate: Why experts want Texas star to stay in school through 2027
articles.standfirst: The Longhorns QB remains a top NFL prospect, but Robert Griffin III believes he needs more time before making the jump to the next level.
articles.summary: The Longhorns QB remains a top NFL prospect, but Robert Griffin III believes he needs more time before making the jump to the next level.
articles.body:
Arch Manning is the starting quarterback for the nation's No. 1 team , but he still hasn't fully convinced with his play this season, even as all eyes in the NFL are on him.

After a slow start, the Texas quarterback closed out his 2025 campaign with 3,163 passing yards, 399 rushing yards and 36 total touchdowns . There were moments when he looked like a true first-round NFL Draft prospect .

Through four games this year, Manning has completed 63.5% of his passes for 862 yards , with seven touchdowns and three interceptions . He has been efficient in wins over Ohio State and Tennessee , but he hasn't yet made the leap many expected, the one that could establish him as the true top prospect.

Appearing on "The Herd" on Tuesday, Robert Griffin III , a former NFL quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner , recommended that Manning return to Texas for the 2027 season . In the former player's view, we haven't seen enough spectacular plays from the talented passer.

"I believe he should come back for another year," Griffin said. "When guys are ready to go to the NFL, playing college football looks easy for them. For myself when I came out, when Andrew Luck came out, it looked easy in our last years. It doesn't look easy for Arch yet."

Will Arch Manning stay one more year in Austin?

Before the 2026 season began, former ESPN analyst Todd McShay had already suggested that Manning could stay one more year with head coach Steve Sarkisian.

"I don't even know that the Mannings are looking at this as the swan song at Texas," said McShay. "There's a long history of Manning sticking around that extra year that people didn't think they were going to stick around until they're right and they feel like they're ready. I won't be surprised at all if he's in the 2028 draft."

It's still too early to speculate about Manning's future , but it's clear he hasn't yet lived up to the enormous expectations that follow him.

Even so, if he decides to declare for the 2027 draft, he will surely have teams interested because of his age, his potential and the weight of his last name in football.

articles.title: Who is Peyton Blomquist? The Gators fan that went viral during game against Ole Miss
articles.standfirst: The University of Florida student became an unexpected talking point after ABC cameras focused on her during the Gators’ 52-28 victory
articles.summary: The University of Florida student became an unexpected talking point after ABC cameras focused on her during the Gators’ 52-28 victory
articles.body:
Florida had plenty to celebrate after improving to 4-0 with a convincing victory over No.4 Ole Miss , but one of the most viral moments from the college football game had nothing to do with a touchdown or defensive stop.

During the ABC broadcast, cameras lingered on a Florida fan in the stands for noticeably longer than a typical crowd shot. Viewers quickly took notice, and social media users began asking, who was the Gators fan on television?

The woman was soon identified as Peyton Blomquist , a first-year University of Florida student who had already built a modest social media presence before the game. Her brief television appearance quickly pushed that attention to a much larger audience.

Peyton Blomquist already active on social media

Blomquist is studying nutritional science at the University of Florida and was among the Gators supporters watching Florida’s 52-28 win over Ole Miss .

She wasn't entirely unfamiliar with online attention before the broadcast. Her Instagram account already featured parts of her life as a Florida student and Gators fan, giving followers a glimpse into her college experience.

The ABC camera shot changed the scale of that attention. As the broadcast remained focused on her, viewers began sharing screenshots and clips across social media.

Fans soon worked out her identity, leading to an influx of interest in her online accounts after the game.

Blomquist later leaned into the moment herself, sharing a recap of Florida’s victory on Instagram and acknowledging her unexpected appearance during the national broadcast. The timing could hardly have been better from a Gators perspective.

Florida’s impressive win over a highly ranked Ole Miss team gave supporters plenty to celebrate, and Blomquist ’s reaction from the stands became part of the wider conversation surrounding the result.

Blomquist has strong academic background

The attention also led fans to learn more about Blomquist away from football. Information shared after the viral moment highlighted an accomplished academic record.

Blomquist graduated as salutatorian before attending Florida and was involved in several school organizations, including ChemClub, the Biology and Medicine Club and multiple honor societies.

She was also involved in debate, adding to a background that suggests her interests extend well beyond sports and social media. Still, it was one unexpected camera shot that introduced her to a much wider audience.

Viral crowd moments have become a familiar part of major college football broadcasts, particularly when fans quickly identify the people shown on screen and send their social media profiles into the spotlight.

Blomquist became the latest example. Florida left the game with a statement win and an unbeaten record, while Blomquist left with thousands of viewers suddenly asking who she was.

articles.title: Student who went viral at Florida vs. Ole Miss is found on Instagram and makes the most of her moment
articles.standfirst: Does the Florida college student have more than her outfits to capitalize on her viral fame?
articles.summary: Does the Florida college student have more than her outfits to capitalize on her viral fame?
articles.body:
College football fans wanted to know who she was. Peyton Blomquist gave them an answer on Instagram. After appearing during ABC’s broadcast of Florida’s September 26 win over Ole Miss, the University of Florida freshman shared game-day photos and footage of her television appearance. Her post made it easy for viewers to recognize the student whose brief moment in the stands had spread across social media.

Her account, @peytonblomquist, showed 53,000 followers when checked for this article, up from fewer than 10,000 before the clip circulated. In her September 27 post, she wore the same outfit seen during the game and included the caption “Work the cut.” She also acknowledged her broadcast appearance with “Go Gators!” on her Instagram Story. Those posts suggest she is comfortable sharing the moment, although she has not publicly explained a broader strategy for her new audience.

Who is Peyton Blomquist beyond the viral NCAA football clip?

Blomquist’s academic interests offer another reason to look beyond the broadcast. Her LinkedIn profile describes her as a University of Florida pre-med student studying nutritional science. She is also a member of the Zeta Tau Alpha sorority.

The New York Post reported that she graduated as salutatorian at her high school in Lake Mary, Florida. For followers discovering her through a football clip , that background introduces a student with plans that were already underway before the sudden attention.

Sport & State reported that it contacted Blomquist about her viral moment and what comes next , but had not received a response when its September 28 story was published. Her Instagram captions acknowledge the attention; they do not amount to an announcement that she intends to become a full-time influencer.

A larger audience could give her room to explore sponsored content, share her college experience or introduce followers to her interests in nutrition and medicine. Those are possibilities, rather than plans she has disclosed. The more interesting question now is whether people who arrived because of a few seconds on television will stay for what she chooses to share afterward.

Posting the game-day outfit helped connect her name to the video. Building something lasting would depend on her own interests and an audience willing to get to know her.

For Florida fans, the next game is already approaching. The Gators beat then-No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 to improve to 4-0, including 2-0 in SEC play.

They visit Missouri on October 3, return to Gainesville to host South Carolina on October 10, and travel to Texas on October 17. Blomquist’s viral appearance came during a major win for her university, and her new followers may now tune in to the next game hoping to spot her in the stands, just as the camera operator did on live television.

Sport & State reported that it contacted Blomquist about her viral moment and what comes next , but had not received a response when its September 28 story was published. Her Instagram captions acknowledge the attention; they do not amount to an announcement that she intends to become a full-time influencer.

A larger audience could give her room to explore sponsored content, share her college experience or introduce followers to her interests in nutrition and medicine. Those are possibilities, rather than plans she has disclosed. The more interesting question now is whether people who arrived because of a few seconds on television will stay for what she chooses to share afterward.
Posting the game-day outfit helped connect her name to the video. Building something lasting would depend on her own interests and an audience willing to get to know her.
For Florida fans, the next game is already approaching. The Gators beat then-No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 to improve to 4-0, including 2-0 in SEC play.

They visit Missouri on October 3, return to Gainesville to host South Carolina on October 10, and travel to Texas on October 17. Blomquist’s viral appearance came during a major win for her university, and her new followers may now tune in to the next game hoping to spot her in the stands, just as the camera operator did on live television.

articles.title: Ryan Day unpacks why Jeremiah Smith is an NFL Draft unicorn
articles.standfirst: The WR is rewriting the rules at Ohio State. The young receiver continues to dominate, and Ryan Day revealed the traits that make him a unique talent and a serious Heisman Trophy contender.
articles.summary: The WR is rewriting the rules at Ohio State. The young receiver continues to dominate, and Ryan Day revealed the traits that make him a unique talent and a serious Heisman Trophy contender.
articles.body:
J eremiah Smith ’s talent is unique, and right now, he is one of the top favorites to win the Heisman Trophy in a season where he continues to prove that he is one of the biggest stars in all of college football. The Ohio State wide receiver has already recorded nearly half of the production he posted throughout the entire previous campaign and remains one of the top offensive weapons for the undefeated Buckeyes.

Ryan Day reveals what makes Jeremiah Smith different

Given the situation, Ohio State head coach Ryan Day did not hesitate to explain what sets his star receiver apart, especially as Smith is projected to be one of the top selections in the NFL Draft .

“What separates him is the mindset, the discipline, and then the skill set,” Day said.

Day highlighted that Smith possesses all the physical and technical qualities needed to become one of the best players in the country.

“It’s hard to discredit the fact that he’s really big and really strong and really fast and powerful, and has really good hand-eye coordination,” he added.

The coach also shared the advice he constantly gives his young star.

“We talk about it all the time. You can’t control how much talent you have. You can only control your discipline and skill.”

A season with elite numbers

After surpassing 1,200 receiving yards in each of his first two seasons, Smith is on pace to break all of his career marks in 2026.

Through just four games, he has recorded 33 receptions for 617 yards and seven touchdowns, while averaging 18.7 yards per catch, the highest mark of his career.

In 2025 , he finished with 87 receptions, 1,243 yards and 12 touchdowns , while during his freshman season in 2024, he posted 76 catches, 1,315 yards and 15 touchdowns — numbers that remain the best of his career in terms of yardage and scoring.

With Ohio State undefeated and once again in contention for a national championship, Smith will face another major test this Saturday when the No. 6 Buckeyes travel to take on the No. 14 Iowa Hawkeyes . The matchup could further strengthen his Heisman Trophy candidacy and continue establishing him as one of the best wide receivers in the country.

articles.title: Dylan Stewart causes uproar in South Carolina: Fans ‘give away’ their jerseys and call for coach's dismissal
articles.standfirst: Star defender still viewed as an elite prospect, but his response to coaches has changed the conversation
articles.summary: Star defender still viewed as an elite prospect, but his response to coaches has changed the conversation
articles.body:
Dylan Stewart entered the season viewed as one of college football ’s most gifted young defenders. After a chaotic loss to Alabama, however, his NFL projection now comes with a very different kind of scrutiny.

The South Carolina edge rusher was suspended indefinitely by coach Shane Beamer after a game in which he was penalized multiple times, swung at Alabama tight end Josh Ford and later resisted attempts by coaches to remove him from the field.

Todd McShay believes that sequence will matter to NFL scouts.

“The thing that concerned me, quite honestly, is it was a dumb mistake to go and have the personal foul penalty or the unnecessary roughness penalty,” McShay said.

“It’s the behavior afterwards. It was unhinged. It felt really unhinged. And that was concerning.”

Bigger issue came after the penalties

The most damaging part of Stewart ’s night may not have been the punch itself. Late in the fourth quarter, freshman Julian Walker was sent in to replace Stewart .

Stewart waved him off, pushed him away and remained on the field until multiple South Carolina coaches became involved.

“It was just the disrespect to Shane Beamer, your head coach, the disrespect to the assistant coaches,” McShay said. “As an [NFL] evaluator, the talent is explosive. He is elite. But evaluators are trying to figure this out: what are we bringing in?”

Beamer made a similar distinction when announcing the suspension: “There’s a standard of how we do things in our program,” he said. “It’s beyond the punch. The punch is unacceptable.

“But it’s some of the other stuff that isn’t how we do things in this program. Accountability is a core value of this program, and we are all accountable to the standard.”

Elite talent no longer only part of evaluation

Stewart ’s physical upside remains obvious. He recorded 6.5 sacks as a freshman in 2024 and 4.5 more in 2025, building a reputation as an explosive edge defender with the burst, flexibility and pass-rush repertoire NFL teams often target early in the draft.

That's why the incident stands out. Josh Pate described the Alabama game as one of the most damaging performances he could remember from a player with Stewart ’s level of talent.

“If Dylan Stewart entered Saturday’s game with the goal of completely tanking his draft stock, I don’t know that he would’ve done anything different than what I watched,” Pate said.

“One of the most self-destructive nights I can remember seeing an elite talent have.”

Beamer has framed the suspension as a chance for Stewart to learn rather than simply a punishment.

“The right thing to do is the hard thing to do, and that’s to sit him down,” Beamer said.

Stewart ’s ceiling hasn't suddenly disappeared. Neither has the athletic ability that made him a potential first-round pick. What has changed is the evaluation around him.

articles.summary: Alabama-Mississippi State and Ohio State-Iowa headline a packed weekend stretching from Friday through early Sunday
articles.body:
College football moves into another major weekend with undefeated teams, ranked matchups and conference races beginning to take shape across the country.

No.7 Alabama ’s trip to No.16 Mississippi State is one of the standout games, with quarterbacks Keelon Russell and Kamario Taylor both making impressive starts to the season.

Russell has thrown for 1,129 yards and eight touchdowns, while Taylor enters with 1,192 yards and a nation-leading 14 touchdown passes.

There's also a major Big Ten matchup in Iowa City, where No.14 Iowa hosts No.5 Ohio State after the Hawkeyes’ dramatic last-second victory over Michigan.

Biggest games to watch in Week 5

Florida ’s visit to Missouri gives Saturday another ranked SEC matchup, while Miami travels to Clemson and BYU faces TCU later in the slate.

articles.title: Arch Manning has answered Texas biggest challenges but an even tougher stretch awaits after the Longhorns’ bye
articles.standfirst: Five of the Longhorns' next six games are against teams that are currently ranked in the top 25
articles.summary: Five of the Longhorns' next six games are against teams that are currently ranked in the top 25
articles.body:
After missing the playoffs last season for the first time since 2023 , head coach Steve Sarkisian and star quarterback Arch Manning entered the 2026 college football season with heavy expectations and a score to settle with the Texas Longhorns .

They have engineered an exceptional start to the opening month, capturing an undefeated record (4-0) highlighted by a statement victory over Ohio State while reigning as the top-ranked team in the nation heading into their early bye week.

The roster has demonstrated impressive balance across both sides of the ball, but the ultimate test lies immediately ahead following the bye, featuring a brutal gauntlet where five of their next six games come against ranked opponents , punctuated by the legendary Red River Rivalry against the Oklahoma Sooners next week.

Arch Manning Overcomes Slow Stats With Clutch Play as Tougher SEC Gauntlet Looms

For now, Arch Manning remains firmly on track as a projected first-round NFL Draft pick should he declare after the season, showing noticeable growth from last year by stepping up when the lights shine brightest, such as orchestrating a stunning 20-point comeback against Ohio State in Week 2.

Through the first four games of his senior campaign, Manning's traditional box scores might not immediately scream Heisman frontrunner, but his underlying impact tells a different story.

The junior signal-caller is currently completing 63.5 percent of his passes for 862 yards and seven touchdowns against three interceptions, while adding 82 rushing yards on 32 carries .

Team-wise, Texas ranks No. 57 nationally in scoring at 33.3 points per game , alongside 147.25 rushing yards per game (93rd) and No. 71 in passing .

Yet, while his aggregate numbers remain modest, Manning shines in high-pressure moments: according to CFBStats.com , he is completing a scorching 76.9 percent of his passes for 115 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter, drastically outperforming his early-game splits and playing flawless, mistake-free football when the Longhorns require a late-game rescue.

Following the bye and the showdown with Oklahoma, Texas faces an unforgiving stretch featuring home matchups against Florida (No. 8) , Ole Miss (No. 9) , and Mississippi State (No. 16) , alongside daunting road trips to Missouri (No. 25) and LSU (No. 11) .

Undeniably, Texas is navigating one of the most grueling schedules in the entire NCAA.

If Manning and the Longhorns emerge from this heavy-metal stretch unscathed or with a single blemish, his draft stock will skyrocket, cementing him as the undisputed favorite to go first overall just like his illustrious uncles, Peyton and Eli .

articles.title: Dave Portnoy out of the Big Noon Kickoff: He points the finger at the one responsible for the decision
articles.standfirst: Barstool Sports is out of Fox’s Saturday pregame coverage, but its relationship with the network continues
articles.summary: Barstool Sports is out of Fox’s Saturday pregame coverage, but its relationship with the network continues
articles.body:
Dave Portnoy and Barstool Sports are no longer part of Fox Sports’ “Big Noon Kickoff,” ending their involvement with the Saturday college football pregame show after a little more than a year.

The decision was first reported by The Athletic’s Andrew Marchand, with sources familiar with the situation saying there wasn’t one specific incident behind the move.

However, it appears the challenge of combining Fox’s more traditional sports presentation with Barstool’s provocative style reportedly became increasingly difficult to sustain. Fox declined to comment publicly on the change.

Portnoy , however, offered his own explanation almost immediately. The Barstool founder claimed Ohio State and head coach Ryan Day pressured the Big Ten and Fox over comments he’d made, ultimately contributing to his removal from the program.

“Ohio State and Ryan Day b****hed and moaned to the Big 10 and threatened Fox till they had no choice,” Portnoy wrote on X.

“Juice wasn’t worth the squeeze [and] frankly I don’t blame them. Huge dollars at stake and you have Cryin Ryan throwing temper tantrums [and] making threats every few days on something I said. I always knew Ryan Day was soft but holy s*** even I didn’t realize he was this soft.

“The Barstool College Football will continue on. Maybe we’ll even see you in Columbus where contrary to popular belief most fans love the rivalry and aren’t p****** like Cryin Ryan.”

Those claims haven’t been publicly confirmed by either Ohio State or Fox. Ohio State officials have instead referred questions about the latest decision to Fox, which hasn’t provided a detailed explanation.

Portnoy’s Ohio State history adds another layer

The dispute is particularly notable because Portnoy is a Michigan graduate, booster and outspoken supporter of the Wolverines. His presence around Ohio State has already created controversy.

When Portnoy made his “Big Noon Kickoff” debut in Columbus in August 2025, he appeared in front of the Buckeyes crowd wearing a shirt mocking Ohio State’s record against Michigan.

He later claimed that Ohio State had banned him from entering Ohio Stadium. The university rejected that characterization, explaining that Fox had decided Portnoy wouldn’t be part of the show’s main desk inside the stadium.

The latest decision comes as “Big Noon Kickoff” travels to Minneapolis for Michigan’s matchup with Minnesota, meaning Portnoy’s first absence coincides with a broadcast centered on his alma mater.

Despite the split, Barstool’s relationship with Fox isn’t completely over. “Wake Up Barstool,” the weekday FS1 program featuring Barstool personalities, remains on the network’s schedule. Portnoy has also indicated that Barstool’s own college football production will continue, potentially including a future stop in Columbus.

Portnoy , however, offered his own explanation almost immediately. The Barstool founder claimed Ohio State and head coach Ryan Day pressured the Big Ten and Fox over comments he’d made, ultimately contributing to his removal from the program.
“Ohio State and Ryan Day b****hed and moaned to the Big 10 and threatened Fox till they had no choice,” Portnoy wrote on X.

“Juice wasn’t worth the squeeze [and] frankly I don’t blame them. Huge dollars at stake and you have Cryin Ryan throwing temper tantrums [and] making threats every few days on something I said. I always knew Ryan Day was soft but holy s*** even I didn’t realize he was this soft.
“The Barstool College Football will continue on. Maybe we’ll even see you in Columbus where contrary to popular belief most fans love the rivalry and aren’t p****** like Cryin Ryan.”

Those claims haven’t been publicly confirmed by either Ohio State or Fox. Ohio State officials have instead referred questions about the latest decision to Fox, which hasn’t provided a detailed explanation.
Portnoy’s Ohio State history adds another layer
The dispute is particularly notable because Portnoy is a Michigan graduate, booster and outspoken supporter of the Wolverines. His presence around Ohio State has already created controversy.
When Portnoy made his “Big Noon Kickoff” debut in Columbus in August 2025, he appeared in front of the Buckeyes crowd wearing a shirt mocking Ohio State’s record against Michigan.

He later claimed that Ohio State had banned him from entering Ohio Stadium. The university rejected that characterization, explaining that Fox had decided Portnoy wouldn’t be part of the show’s main desk inside the stadium.
The latest decision comes as “Big Noon Kickoff” travels to Minneapolis for Michigan’s matchup with Minnesota, meaning Portnoy’s first absence coincides with a broadcast centered on his alma mater.

Despite the split, Barstool’s relationship with Fox isn’t completely over. “Wake Up Barstool,” the weekday FS1 program featuring Barstool personalities, remains on the network’s schedule. Portnoy has also indicated that Barstool’s own college football production will continue, potentially including a future stop in Columbus.

articles.title: Northwestern spent $875 million on a smaller stadium. Opening night explained why
articles.summary: Northwestern did not unveil its new home quietly. The Wildcats opened the $875 million Ryan Field on Friday night against Penn State, turning the first game in their new stadium into a spectacle, and then making the night even more memorable with a 34-13 victory over the Nittany Lions. The new Ryan Field is unlike most major college football stadium projects. Northwestern spent more money than any college program has previously spent on a stadium while intentionally reducing its capacity to 35,000, making it the smallest venue in the Big Ten. The philosophy is clear: fewer seats, closer fans, louder football.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders is Coach Prime's “executioner” in Colorado: The big problem that could lead to his father's firing
articles.standfirst: Colorado's latest quarterback gamble has failed badly, leaving Deion Sanders facing a familiar problem that could ultimately determine whether he remains in Boulder
articles.summary: Colorado's latest quarterback gamble has failed badly, leaving Deion Sanders facing a familiar problem that could ultimately determine whether he remains in Boulder
articles.body:
D eion Sanders has spent much of his Colorado tenure trying to convince everyone that the program is moving forward.

The latest evidence suggests he still has one major problem to solve, and it happens to be the position his son Shedeur Sanders once controlled.

Colorado's 29-7 home defeat to No. 12 Texas Tech on Saturday was not simply another loss for a team that has already endured a difficult 2026 season. It was another reminder that the Buffaloes have not found a reliable answer at quarterback since Shedeur left for the NFL .

That is becoming a significant concern for Sanders .

Colorado is now 2-3, with three defeats in its last three games. The latest setback was particularly damaging because the Buffaloes had opportunities to win, leading 7-3 at halftime and holding Texas Tech to relatively modest offensive production for much of the contest. Instead, the game unraveled after the break.

Isaac Wilson , who was handed the starting job after Julian Lewis was removed from the lineup, could not maintain the momentum generated by Colorado's opening touchdown drive.

The Utah transfer threw three interceptions, with his final mistake becoming a pick-six that effectively put the game beyond reach. Texas Tech ultimately scored 29 unanswered points.

The quarterback situation therefore looks less like an isolated problem and more like an unresolved issue that has followed Sanders since Shedeur's departure.

The Shedeur comparison is becoming impossible to avoid

Shedeur's presence in Boulder provided Colorado with something the team has repeatedly lacked since 2024: continuity.

The Buffaloes went 9-4 that season, with Shedeur operating as the clear starter and one of the central figures in Sanders ' rebuilding project. Since then, Colorado has gone through multiple quarterbacks without finding the same level of consistency.

Last season ended with a 3-9 record and three different starting quarterbacks. This season has now brought another change, with Wilson replacing Lewis after Lewis opened the year as the starter.

Wilson's performance against Texas Tech made the situation even more complicated.

He completed 26 of 44 passes for 290 yards and a touchdown, but his three interceptions proved decisive.

The Red Raiders converted Colorado's mistakes into points while the Buffaloes' offense repeatedly failed to sustain drives. The official Colorado account confirmed that the Buffaloes fell to 2-3 overall and 0-2 in Big 12 play after the defeat.

Wilson accepted responsibility afterward.

“It’s me,” Wilson said. “I had my chance tonight.” He later added: “I did not make smart decisions tonight.”

That leaves Sanders with another difficult decision during Colorado's bye week. “It’s always an open competition,” Sanders said.

The problem is that changing quarterbacks again may not fix everything. Colorado's struggles extend beyond the player taking snaps. Its offense has repeatedly failed to turn promising situations into points, while the defense has been forced to carry an enormous burden.

Against Texas Tech, Colorado actually outgained the Red Raiders 375-315, yet still lost by 22 points.

That imbalance is precisely why pressure is building around Sanders .

The Buffaloes have already been identified as a potential hot-seat situation for their head coach, with Sanders' record at Colorado and last year's 3-9 campaign adding to the scrutiny.

His contract also makes any decision complicated: Colorado extended him through 2029, and reports have put the potential 2026 buyout at around $25.5 million.

That financial figure could make an immediate dismissal difficult, but it does not eliminate the underlying question.

Can Sanders get Colorado back to being competitive?

The answer may depend heavily on whether he can finally solve the quarterback position.

His next opportunity comes against No. 13 Utah on Oct. 17 following the bye week. By then, Sanders will have had time to assess Wilson's performance, reconsider Lewis and potentially explore freshman Kaneal Sweetwyne , who has yet to make a start.

There is also pressure on the coaching staff to find a better offensive formula. Saturday's loss exposed how little margin for error Colorado currently has: the defense can keep a ranked opponent within striking distance, but repeated offensive mistakes eventually become impossible to overcome. Sanders knows that better than anyone.

“Let’s stop the shenanigans, man,” Sanders told reporters. “We’ve got one glaring problem. You guys know darn well what that is. Let’s stop the foolishness. We’ve got to play better at one specific position. That’s it.”

He refused to directly name quarterback when asked about the team's problems.

"If I say it you're gonna run with it," he said. He then told reporters, “I’d respect y’all a lot more if you just said it yourself."

The message was clear without Sanders needing to say the word. Shedeur is gone, but his absence continues to loom over the Colorado offense.

For Coach Prime, finding the next quarterback is no longer simply about improving one position. It could determine whether his rebuilding project survives another difficult season, and ultimately whether he remains the person in charge of it.

articles.title: Deion Sanders challenges Julian ‘Juju’ Lewis to tell the truth about his difficult situation in Colorado
articles.standfirst: Coach Prime insists Julian Lewis' demotion is more complicated than a simple benching as Colorado searches for answers after another offensive collapse
articles.summary: Coach Prime insists Julian Lewis' demotion is more complicated than a simple benching as Colorado searches for answers after another offensive collapse
articles.body:
D eion Sanders is not prepared to provide the full explanation behind Julian “JuJu” Lewis ' sudden fall down the Colorado quarterback depth chart.

Instead, the Buffaloes coach has effectively put the responsibility back on Lewis to explain his side of the story.

Colorado entered the 2026 season expecting Lewis to be one of the central figures in its offense.

The highly regarded quarterback started the first four games, but his performances became increasingly inconsistent before Sanders replaced him during the loss to Baylor .

That decision has now developed into a much bigger storyline.

Against No. 12 Texas Tech on Saturday, Oct. 3, Lewis was not merely replaced by Isaac Wilson. He was listed behind Wilson and another quarterback, leaving him as the apparent third option at the position.

Sanders pushed back strongly against the suggestion that he simply benched Lewis and moved him to third string: "I would love for JuJu to come in here and he tells you what happened. You bench JuJu to third or second string? No that's not how it all went down. It didn't happen like that."

Those comments have only added another layer to an already complicated quarterback situation.

Sanders clearly does not want to publicly blame a 19-year-old player, but he also does not appear interested in accepting responsibility for a narrative that he believes does not accurately explain Lewis ' situation.

Lewis had shown flashes of why Colorado viewed him as an important part of the program's future.

He threw for 366 yards and four touchdowns while adding another score on the ground against Weber State earlier this season, earning Big 12 freshman of the week honors in the process.

However, his production dipped in the weeks that followed. He was replaced at halftime against Baylor after completing 11 of 16 passes for only 75 yards, with Wilson entering and providing an immediate spark.

Wilson subsequently received the start against Texas Tech. The change initially looked promising.

Wilson's opportunity creates another problem for Sanders

Wilson opened the Texas Tech game by leading Colorado on a 75-yard touchdown drive, giving the Buffaloes exactly the offensive spark Sanders had hoped to find.

But the momentum disappeared, and Wilson ultimately threw three interceptions as Texas Tech turned the contest into a 29-7 victory.

That result has left Sanders with no obvious solution: "It's always competition everyday. Every day is like that. We have three options there [at quarterback], somebody just has to grab a hold of it and get it done."

The phrase “three options” is significant because it suggests Lewis remains part of the conversation despite his unusual status against Texas Tech .

Sanders was also careful not to publicly attack Lewis: "JuJu didn't play today. But I'm not going to badger the kid or say anything derogatory about the kid. He didn't play today. I'm more worried about our team. You're trying to single out a kid and I can't do that. These kids are pretty darn comfortable."

That approach is understandable given the scrutiny surrounding Colorado's offense. Lewis is still young and remains a significant part of the program's long-term plans, while publicly damaging his confidence could create an even bigger problem for a team already searching for stability.

Yet Sanders ' patience is also being tested by the results.

The loss to Texas Tech dropped Colorado to 2-3, while the Buffaloes have now lost three straight games. The offense has become the most obvious weakness, even though the defense has produced strong stretches against quality opposition.

Sanders made no attempt to disguise his frustration: "We've been horrible. I won't sugarcoat it. We had seven points? You're not going to win."

Colorado's offensive problems were particularly frustrating against Texas Tech because the Buffaloes were competitive for much of the game.

The Red Raiders entered the fourth quarter with only a 12-7 advantage before Colorado's mistakes opened the door for a decisive late run.

"[Texas Tech] knows how to win. They don't panic, or flinch and they're consistent at what they do. It's funny because when you look at the statisitics, it doesn't tell the story of the game,” Sanders said.

"It was 12-7 in the fourth quarter. Then all hell breaks loose. Hats off to Texas Tech. They played a wonderful game and did what they had to do to get the win. We didn't."

The numbers also underline the strange nature of Colorado's defeat. Texas Tech was held to limited passing production, while Colorado's defense generated pressure and kept the game close deep into the contest.

But four interceptions, three from Wilson and another on a trick play, ultimately proved too costly.

Sanders knows that quarterback play has to improve, but he does not believe the team's problems can simply be placed on one individual: "You know what it is. If I said it, you're going to run with it. You know darn well what it is. Write it yourselves. It's blatant. I would respect it a lot more if you wrote down what it is."

"You want me to take me down that rabbit hole or bunjee jump on it? Just say what you want to say and write what you want to write. Because if I assist you, it sounds like blame. It's a team effort. We all got our butt kicks."

The bye week now gives Sanders time to make another decision.

He could stick with Wilson, restore Lewis to the starting role or potentially give another quarterback an opportunity.

But after Wilson's collapse against Texas Tech, the quarterback debate is unlikely to disappear: It's execution. There's no way you can go down the field on the first drive and and score like that, and then you can't anymore. It's also want and will."

Sanders also insisted that effort is not the issue: “We're going to practice and we're going to work."

"We were ready to play today. It's not like we weren't ready. Defense did some phenomenal things today and the offense [too]. They work. It's not for lack of effort."

The next test comes against No. 13 Utah on Oct. 17, giving Sanders two weeks to decide who he believes can finally provide consistency at quarterback.

For Lewis , that means his difficult situation is far from resolved. Sanders has refused to publicly define exactly why his young quarterback has fallen down the depth chart.

Instead, he has challenged Lewis to tell his own story. At the same time, Sanders knows that the larger issue cannot be avoided forever: "I like many aspects of it. But we were penalized on a crucial drive and we broke at the end."

"A great defense does not break. They don't consistently miss tackles. We got one glaring problem and you guys know what it is. I ain't no fool. We have one glaring problem. We have to play better at one specific position [quarterback]. That's it."

And until Colorado finds a definitive answer under center, the Lewis situation will continue to be one of the biggest questions hanging over Sanders and his program.

articles.title: Approved by Regina George! Jordon Hudson rocks pink alongside Bill Belichick for 'Mean Girls' Day
articles.standfirst: Hudson used October 3 to make a carefully timed pop-culture reference
articles.summary: Hudson used October 3 to make a carefully timed pop-culture reference
articles.body:
Jordon Hudson has made a habit of drawing attention with her game-day outfits, but Saturday’s look came with an extra layer of meaning.

The girlfriend of North Carolina head coach Bill Belichick wore a baby pink silk corset with matching wide-leg trousers as UNC faced Notre Dame, pairing the outfit with oversized glasses and a pink bedazzled football-shaped handbag.

The timing was hard to miss. October 3 has become closely associated with Mean Girls because of a scene in which Cady Heron , played by Lindsay Lohan, recalls a brief interaction with her crush Aaron Samuels .

“On October 3rd, he asked me what day it was,” Cady says in the film. “It’s October 3rd.”

That line has turned the date into an annual reference point for fans of the movie, while pink is also central to the film because of the Plastics’ rule: “On Wednesdays, we wear pink.”

Hudson look carried clear pop-culture theme

Hudson ’s outfit appeared to combine both references while still keeping a football connection through the sparkling handbag. It also followed another eye-catching appearance earlier in the season.

It also followed another eye-catching appearance earlier in the season. At UNC’s Sept. 19 game against Clemson, Hudson wore a strapless baby blue jumpsuit with ruffled detailing, matching the school’s colors.

She completed that look with white heels and a small white bag. Hudson has otherwise been relatively quiet on social media in recent months.

Her last post came in June, when she and Belichick attended the Kentucky Derby together.

Hudson continues to appear alongside Belichick

Her public support for Belichick hasn't been limited to home games. Hudson also traveled with him during a recent high school scouting trip, joining him in Maryland on September 25 to watch Archbishop Spalding face Gilman from the press box.

The couple have been dating since 2023, and Hudson has remained a visible presence as Belichick continues his transition from the NFL to college football. Saturday’s result, however, didn't go North Carolina’s way.

UNC fell 37-26 to Notre Dame , extending the Tar Heels ’ losing streak to two games. Belichick ’s team now turns its attention to Pittsburgh next week, with another opportunity to steady the season.

Hudson , meanwhile, managed to create one of the day’s most talked-about fashion moments before the final score was even settled. The pink corset wasn't simply a game-day choice. On October 3, it was a very deliberate Mean Girls reference.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith is done being modest. He's coming for the Heisman Trophy
articles.standfirst: The Buckeyes' recent run has elevated the conversation in college football
articles.summary: The Buckeyes' recent run has elevated the conversation in college football
articles.body:
J eremiah Smith i sn't interested in letting anyone else decide who the best player in college football is. He's making the argument himself. After another spectacular performance Saturday, the Ohio State wide receiver delivered a message to Heisman voters that was as direct as his production has been all season.

"You've just got to [let] the Heisman voters or whoever it is know that I'm the best player in the country," Smith said, via ESPN's Adam Rittenberg . "I've got to be there." At this point, it is getting increasingly difficult to dismiss the claim.

Smith caught 11 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns as No. 5 Ohio State overwhelmed No. 14 Iowa 31-14 at Kinnick Stadium. The junior receiver wasn't simply productive; he was the central figure in a nationally significant road victory. And this wasn't an isolated performance.

A week earlier against Illinois, Smith caught 12 passes for 217 yards and four touchdowns. In his past two games, he has totaled 23 receptions, 423 yards and six touchdowns. That is absurd production.

Smith is turning dominance into a Heisman argument

Smith entered the season as one of the most recognizable players in college football, but his recent run has elevated the conversation. Through Ohio State's first five games, Smith has 44 receptions for 823 yards and nine touchdowns, according to the supplied statistics. Those numbers put him at or near the top of the national leaderboard in all three major receiving categories.

Against Iowa, Smith also added another chapter to his Ohio State legacy. His two touchdown receptions gave him 36 career receiving touchdowns, moving him past Chris Olave for the most in program history. His 11 catches also pushed his career total to 207, surpassing Emeka Egbuka's previous school record. articles.title: Nikola Jokic and Nuggets teammates head to Boulder for the Deion Sanders experience.
articles.summary: Nikola Jokic is usually not the NBA superstar looking for the spotlight. On Saturday night, he was perfectly happy to take it in. The Denver Nuggets' three-time MVP brought several teammates to Folsom Field to watch Deion Sanders and Colorado take on No. 12 Texas Tech, turning a college football game into an early-season team-bonding opportunity. Jokic's presence was notable for another reason: his relationship with Sanders has come a long way. Not long ago, Jokic acknowledged that he didn't even know who "Prime Time" was. Now, the Nuggets center was sitting in the stands watching Sanders coach Colorado alongside members of his own team.

articles.title: Bill Belichick's tension during his interview with Taylor McGregor is about to boil over
articles.standfirst: Another uncomfortable sideline interview has put the North Carolina coach under the spotlight after the Tar Heels fell to No. 3 Notre Dame
articles.summary: Another uncomfortable sideline interview has put the North Carolina coach under the spotlight after the Tar Heels fell to No. 3 Notre Dame
articles.body:
B ill Belichick has never been known for giving lengthy or particularly revealing answers during football interviews, but his latest exchange with ESPN's Taylor McGregor became especially awkward because of what happened immediately afterward.

North Carolina was attempting to slow down No. 3 Notre Dame during Saturday's matchup at Kenan Memorial Stadium when McGregor approached Belichick for a brief sideline interview.

The Tar Heels were facing a crucial third-down situation, and the ESPN reporter asked the longtime coach what his defense needed to do to prevent the Fighting Irish from extending their drive.

Belichick appeared visibly irritated by the timing of the question. After staring into the distance for several seconds, he offered a remarkably short response.

“Well, it’s third down, you know. They’re one for two on third down. So, we’ll see how it goes here,” he said. The timing could hardly have been worse.

ESPN returned to the game immediately after the exchange, and Notre Dame converted the third down. The Fighting Irish then found the end zone, turning the moment into an instant talking point on social media.

It was the sort of sequence that made Belichick's terse response look particularly unfortunate, even though there was obviously no way for him to know exactly what would happen on the next play.

Notre Dame ultimately defeated North Carolina 37-26, leaving the Tar Heels at 2-2 on the season. The loss also continued a difficult start to Belichick's second season in Chapel Hill after UNC endured a losing campaign during his first year in charge.

Belichick's relationship with the media is back under the microscope

The incident has reignited a familiar discussion surrounding Belichick's relationship with television interviews.

The six-time Super Bowl-winning coach has spent much of his career answering questions in an extremely direct and economical manner.

That approach was often accepted as part of the Belichick persona during his time with the New England Patriots , when his teams regularly competed for championships. At North Carolina, however, the environment is different.

Belichick is attempting to rebuild a college program while operating under considerably more media scrutiny than he experienced during the NFL season.

Every awkward exchange can become a social-media clip, and Saturday's moment with McGregor was particularly easy for fans to circulate because the game immediately provided an ironic conclusion.

Some college football fans were openly frustrated by the continued use of sideline interviews involving Belichick .

“TV just needs to stop interviewing this miserable (expletive) before, during and after games. (Expletive) media needs to not show up to his pressers as well,” one fan wrote.

“They looked real good on the opening drive and subsequent possession. Things kinda went downhill after that though,” one fan added.

“I don’t think Bill Belichick is long for Chapel Hill, folks. Don’t blame Taylor either,” one fan added.

“Taylor waves the nicest white flag I’ve ever seen when an interview isn’t going the way it’s supposed to,” one fan added.

The criticism of Belichick's demeanor, however, should not obscure what happened on the field.

North Carolina actually began the game well, taking a 7-0 lead before Notre Dame responded with three straight touchdowns.

The Tar Heels closed the gap to 21-14 before halftime and then made the game extremely interesting by opening the second half with a 98-yard kickoff return touchdown from Jaden Jefferson . That cut Notre Dame's lead to 21-20.

The Irish responded with the kind of sustained possession that ultimately decided the contest.

Notre Dame produced a 17-play, 75-yard drive that consumed more than nine minutes of the third quarter, with freshman running back Jonaz Walton carrying the ball 12 times for 61 yards during the possession.

Notre Dame finished with 475 total yards, including 241 on the ground, while North Carolina managed only 285 total yards and 77 rushing yards. Quarterback C.J. Carr completed 21 of 29 passes for 234 yards and four touchdowns, while Walton finished with 120 rushing yards.

Those numbers help explain why the game eventually moved away from the Tar Heels, even after they repeatedly threatened to make it competitive. For Belichick, the bigger issue is now the direction of the program.

A 2-2 record is not disastrous, particularly considering Notre Dame entered the game ranked third nationally and remained unbeaten. UNC also showed enough fight to suggest that the team has made progress in certain areas.

But expectations surrounding Belichick are naturally different from those attached to most first-time college coaches. His NFL résumé created enormous attention when he arrived in Chapel Hill, and the program's struggles have therefore been magnified.

The McGregor interview was ultimately just a few seconds of television. It did not cause Notre Dame to score, and it did not determine the outcome.

Yet because the Fighting Irish immediately converted the situation and eventually won by 11 points, the clip has become another example of how little room Belichick currently has for an uncomfortable moment.

For now, the focus should remain on the football rather than the sideline interview. North Carolina has to respond quickly, with the season moving forward and the pressure surrounding Belichick's tenure unlikely to disappear.

And if the Tar Heels continue to struggle, moments like the one with McGregor will only attract more attention.
