articles.title: Paul Finebaum announces that it's over for Deion Sanders in Colorado: “There's no turning back”
articles.standfirst: Colorado's latest collapse raises questions about whether Coach Prime can recover from a three-game losing streak
articles.summary: Colorado's latest collapse raises questions about whether Coach Prime can recover from a three-game losing streak
articles.body:
Paul Finebaum believes Deion Sanders ' time at Colorado is heading toward an unavoidable conclusion after another damaging defeat exposed the same problems that have followed the Buffaloes throughout the 2026 season.

Colorado 's latest setback came Saturday night, when No.12 Texas Tech overwhelmed the Buffaloes 29-7 at Folsom Field. The result dropped Sanders' team to 2-3 overall and 0-2 in Big 12 play, with Colorado entering its bye week having lost three consecutive games.

For Finebaum , one particular moment summed up the current state of the program.

“When the last image of a program’s last breath is your quarterback in his own end zone throwing a pick six, it’s over,” Finebaum said on The Matt Barrie Show.

“And I am not an ‘I told you so guy,’ and I thought I was wrong when I made this bullish*t statement years ago, and I never liked the move to Colorado… It just didn’t feel right, and I was completely wrong for a while because they bought into it.”

The interception came with Colorado already trailing in the fourth quarter. Isaac Wilson , making his first start for the Buffaloes , attempted a pass from deep in his own territory that Texas Tech linebacker John Curry intercepted for a touchdown.

It turned a difficult night into a 22-7 deficit and effectively ended Colorado's hopes of a comeback. Wilson 's performance was particularly problematic. He finished with 290 passing yards and one touchdown but threw three interceptions.

Colorado also lost the ball on a trick-play interception, meaning the Buffaloes committed four turnovers in total. Texas Tech converted those mistakes into 19 points.

The loss was even more frustrating because Colorado actually looked capable of competing during the opening half.

The Buffaloes scored on their opening possession and carried a 7-3 advantage into halftime. It was Colorado's first halftime lead against an FBS opponent in more than a year. But the offense completely stalled after the break, while Texas Tech scored 29 unanswered points.

Quarterback problem impossible for Sanders to ignore

Sanders has now openly identified quarterback play as the biggest obstacle facing his team.

The coach chose Wilson over Julian "JuJu" Lewis for the Texas Tech game in an attempt to inject life into an offense that had struggled badly. The decision initially appeared promising, but Wilson's three interceptions ultimately became central to the defeat.

Colorado's quarterback situation has been unsettled since Shedeur Sanders left following the 2024 season.

The Buffaloes cycled through three starting quarterbacks during their 3-9 campaign in 2025, and another change has already been made this season. Sanders was blunt after the latest loss.

“That's the position that's somewhat disabling us and disarming us,” he told reporters. “Somebody's got to step up and take hold of it and get it done.”

The coach also said the Buffaloes have "one glaring problem" and challenged his quarterbacks to improve during the bye week. Finebaum, meanwhile, believes the problem extends beyond one position.

“But that is not an easy place to manage,” Finebaum continued. “It is going to end either gracefully or spectacularly badly for Deion. I hate it. I know you do. Everybody does because… I’ve come to really respect and admire him.”

The Buffaloes went 3-9 last season, and this year's three-game skid has quickly erased much of the optimism generated by a 2-0 start. The criticism has also intensified beyond the quarterback position.

Colorado was flagged eight times for 84 yards against Texas Tech , missed two field goals and failed on a fake punt. Finebaum nevertheless made clear that his comments weren't motivated by a lack of respect for Sanders.

“He’s only the most charismatic figure we’ve seen in this game in a long time. But you can’t keep going,” Finebaum concluded. “Even with the beginning of the season that went well for him, nothing has gone right, and you cannot get it back.”

Sanders now has a bye week to find answers before Colorado returns October 17 against Utah.

That break could be particularly important because the Buffaloes need to settle their quarterback situation and find a way to generate consistent offense before the season slips further away. Finebaum has already reached his conclusion.

Whether Colorado 's next few games prove him right remains to be seen, but the pressure on Sanders is undoubtedly increasing.

The coach who once transformed the Buffaloes into one of college football's biggest stories now has to find a way to stop a three-game losing streak and restore an identity that has become increasingly difficult to see on the field.

articles.title: College Football Games Today: Date, time, and where to watch every NCAAF game during Week 6
articles.summary: October has arrived, and with it comes the point in the college football season when conference races and playoff ambitions begin to take on real urgency.
articles.body:
October has arrived, and with it comes the point in the college football season when conference races and playoff ambitions begin to take on real urgency.

Week 6 spreads the action across five days, beginning Tuesday with Southern Miss visiting Troy and continuing through a Saturday schedule featuring many of the biggest programs in the country.

The centerpiece comes in Tuscaloosa, where No.2 Georgia travels to face No.6 Alabama in a game carrying major SEC and national implications. Alabama enters as a narrow home favorite, setting up one of the most closely matched heavyweight contests of the season.

Saturday also brings the Red River rivalry between No.1 Texas and Oklahoma , No.21 UCLA traveling to No.13 Oregon , and No.19 USC heading to Penn State .

All kickoff times below are listed in Eastern Time.

articles.title: Pat McAfee's wife reveals the ESPN host's struggle to protect his family amid death threats
articles.standfirst: The ESPN host refuses to let online threats keep him from a special family moment
articles.summary: The ESPN host refuses to let online threats keep him from a special family moment
articles.body:
Pat McAfee’s weekend took him from the center of college football to a more personal role as a husband and father, with his wife Samantha offering a glimpse of the effort he made to spend time with their daughter despite a demanding schedule and renewed online hostility.

After ESPN’s College GameDay broadcast from Iowa City on October 3, McAfee had little downtime before his Monday Night Football commitments.

Still, Samantha wanted to take their daughter Kenzie to Disney World’s Mickey’s Not-So-Scary Halloween Party. According to her Instagram story, McAfee told her he’d fly in for around 16 hours to make the family outing happen.

He followed through. Samantha shared that McAfee arrived and took Kenzie for a night swim, calling him the “best dad & husband.”

“I told him I wanted to take kenz to the NSSMHP and he said ‘I’ll fly in for like 16 hrs’ He arrived and took kenz on a night swim! Thank you for being the best dad & husband,” she wrote.

The moment was especially memorable for Samantha because she said she’d never seen her husband react that way to a Disney character before. The family has visited Disney World previously, with McAfee sharing a video in February showing Kenzie enjoying a hug with Winnie the Pooh.

However, their latest trip came against a much darker backdrop. On October 4, McAfee shared a hostile Instagram message apparently sparked by his commentary about Notre Dame on College GameDay.

The message contained a direct threat against McAfee and another member of his show, highlighting the disturbing abuse that can accompany his high-profile sports career.

McAfee continues putting family first despite the pressure

The threat wasn’t an isolated incident. McAfee has faced disturbing messages before, including an episode in September when an online commenter referenced the killing of Charlie Kirk while suggesting McAfee should suffer a similar fate.

Such incidents demonstrate the intensity of reactions that can follow the former NFL kicker’s outspoken opinions.

Despite that hostility, the weekend showed that McAfee hasn’t allowed online threats to completely dictate his life. Instead, he made the effort to travel to Disney World, spend time with Kenzie and then return to his professional commitments.

His Iowa appearance also generated controversy for another reason. During College GameDay, McAfee offered $1 million to student Finley Banfig and another $1 million to the University of Iowa Health Care Stead Family Children’s Hospital if she successfully made her field goal.

After Banfig missed, former Iowa tight end Dallas Clark was brought in and successfully threw a football through the uprights, resulting in $150,000 for both Banfig and the hospital. McAfee subsequently faced criticism over the reduced donation.

Rather than ignore the backlash, McAfee admitted that the criticism was fair. On October 5, he announced that he’d donate the full $1 million to the children's hospital, restoring the amount he had originally promised.

Between College GameDay, Monday Night Football, public criticism and threatening messages, McAfee’s schedule remains relentless, but Samantha’s account paints a different picture of the ESPN personality away from the cameras.

articles.title: Deion "Coach Prime" Sanders' Buffaloes have almost nothing left to play for as Utah looms
articles.standfirst: Colorado needs a win to stop its slide, but it is facing one of the conference’s strongest teams
articles.summary: Colorado needs a win to stop its slide, but it is facing one of the conference’s strongest teams
articles.body:
Deion "Coach Prime" Sanders' team is running out of time to salvage its season. ESPN’s latest Football Power Index has Colorado at 0% to win the Big 12, reach the College Football Playoff or capture a national championship.

Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes have received the kind of news that confirms what their recent performances have been suggesting: the road to a meaningful postseason has become almost impossible.

For a program hoping to establish itself as a legitimate contender under Sanders, the projection is another sobering reality check, and a harsh one... which could be an understatement when we talk about one of the most popular head coaches in college football.

It should not come as a surprise

Colorado has lost to Baylor and, most recently, a top-10 Texas Tech team after an earlier defeat against Northwestern. Those results have left the Buffaloes struggling to keep pace with the conference’s leading programs.

Their latest FPI rating tells the story. Colorado sits at -0.5, up slightly from -0.6 last week, but remains at the bottom of the Big 12 rankings . More concerning is the projected record. FPI has Colorado finishing 4.1-7.9, the worst projection in the conference. That would leave the Buffaloes two wins short of bowl eligibility, while their chance of reaching six victories has fallen to just 13.9%.

More concerning is the projected record. FPI has Colorado finishing 4.1-7.9, the worst projection in the conference. That would leave the Buffaloes two wins short of bowl eligibility, while their chance of reaching six victories has fallen to just 13.9%. The numbers leave little room for interpretation: Colorado needs a dramatic turnaround.

That turnaround will not be easy to start. Colorado’s next opponent is Utah, which is tied with Texas Tech as the No. 11 team nationally in FP I and ranks as the highest-rated team in the Big 12.

The Utes are coming to Boulder at exactly the wrong time for Sanders. Colorado needs a win to stop its slide, but it is facing one of the conference’s strongest teams.

A victory would not suddenly restore the Buffaloes’ championship hopes. It would, however, give Sanders something the program desperately needs: evidence that this season can still be salvaged.

Coach Prime needs answers

The latest FPI projection is ultimately a reflection of what has happened on the field. Colorado has not been consistent enough against quality competition, and its margin for error is shrinking by the week.

The task now is much simpler than it was at the beginning of the season for "Coach Prime" and the Buffaloes. The championship conversation is over. Colorado need to start winning, and that mission begins with Utah.

A loss would push Colorado closer to the 4- or 5-win territory projected by FPI and make bowl eligibility even more difficult. A win would not fix everything, but it could provide the momentum needed to change the direction of the season. The numbers have delivered a brutal verdict on Colorado . Now Coach Prime has to find a way to prove them wrong.

articles.title: Nick Saban benching of Jalen Hurts for Tua Tagovailoa resurfaces, and Hurts' response shows why he still succeeded
articles.standfirst: Saban made one of the most consequential halftime decisions in college football history while at Alabama.
articles.summary: Saban made one of the most consequential halftime decisions in college football history while at Alabama.
articles.body:
There were a lot of reasons for why Nick Saban was such a highly successful college football coach. His recruiting was as good as it gets, he surrounded himself with the best possible coaching staffs, and he made tough decisions when they needed to be made for the betterment of the team.

One of those tough decisions stands out above the rest. During the 2018 CFP National Championship , Saban made the call to bench starting quarterback Jalen Hurts at halftime. Alabama was down 13-0 to Georgia at that time , and Saban turned to true freshman Tua Tagovailoa to save the day. Tagovailoa did just that, leading the Crimson Tide to a 26-23 overtime win .

Saban's decision was obviously a polarizing one. Hurts had started all of the team's games up until that point and had turned into one of the best dual threat quarterbacks in the nation. But the Bulldogs defense had thrown him completely off his game.

Nick Saban had thought about benching Jalen Hurts for Tua Tagovailoa for months heading into National Championship

This week, new footage of that consequential moment has surfaced. Taken from the " Saban " documentary on ESPN, it was clear that Hurts was emotionally hurt by the decision in the locker room . Saban admitted it was a "calculated" call, that he had thought about making for nearly two months .

It worked out flawlessly, and Hurts ended up succeeding regardless of that decision . He has already won a Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles - and made another one - and has outlasted Tagovailoa as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Hurts' postgame interview, talking about getting benched, is a good glimpse into why he has been able to overcome it.

Even though Hurts obviously wanted to finish that National Championship game under center, his hard work helped pave the way to winning that title. He had shared the locker room with all of those players, including Tagovailoa, and didn't let his own disappointment affect the rest of the team.

articles.title: Texas Longhorns vs Oklahoma Sooners: Where to watch the Arch Manning game and what time is the Red River Rivalry today?
articles.standfirst: Red River showdown returns: Texas favored as Longhorns and Sooners renew college football's fiercest grudge
articles.summary: Red River showdown returns: Texas favored as Longhorns and Sooners renew college football's fiercest grudge
articles.body:
There are few dates circled more aggressively on the college football calendar than the one that pits the Oklahoma Sooners against the Texas Longhorns. The Red River rivalry — one of the sport's most storied and bitter feuds — is back, and the betting market has already made its leanings clear before a single snap is played. When these two line up, records, rankings, and reputations tend to matter a little less than the raw intensity of the moment.

When and where to watch the Texas Longhorns vs Oklahoma Sooners game?

The College Football matchup is scheduled for this Saturday, October 10, 2026, with a headline kickoff listed at 3:30 p.m. Eastern Time (2:30 p.m. Central Time and 12:30 Pacific Time)

As for the broadcast: you can catch the game local television and through ABC the official competition broadcaster for this game.

Texas Longhorns vs Oklahoma Sooners: Reading between the lines

A spread of eight points paired with a sub-40 total paints a specific picture: the market sees Texas as the more complete side, but it does not anticipate a shootout . That combination — a clear favorite in a low-scoring projection — typically signals a game where one team is expected to control tempo, lean on its ground game, and keep the opposing offense off the field.

For Oklahoma, the path to springing the upset is written all over those numbers. A +8 cushion is exactly the sort of line that rivalry underdogs have a habit of covering, even in defeat.

The Sooners don't need a perfect performance to make this uncomfortable for Texas; they need to win the turnover battle, keep the game in single digits, and let the emotional edge of a hostile, familiar environment do the rest. In a series this charged, favorites are rarely allowed to coast.

For Texas, the challenge is matching the market's expectations rather than merely meeting them. Being favored by more than a touchdown over your archrival is a burden as much as a compliment — it invites the kind of slow start and second-half scramble that defines so many chapters of this rivalry.

The Longhorns will want to establish control early and avoid the trap of letting Oklahoma hang around, because a close game in the fourth quarter of a Red River clash is anyone's game.

What to watch for during the 2026 Red River Rivalry?

The key battlegrounds in a game projected this way almost always come down to a handful of swing factors. First, third-down efficiency: with a total this low, sustaining drives and flipping field position will be at a premium for both sides.

Second, turnovers — the single most reliable upset ingredient for a dog getting more than a touchdown . And third, red-zone finishing; in a game where points may be scarce, the team that turns opportunities into touchdowns rather than field goals will likely be the one celebrating.

The emotional temperature is its own variable. Rivalry games routinely produce performances that defy the pregame numbers, and Oklahoma will be banking on exactly that unpredictability to erase the gap the market has drawn.

The Betting Market's Verdict: Texas the clear favorite

If the bookmakers are to be believed, this one has a decided tilt toward the visitors. The betting board installs the Texas Longhorns as strong favorites, with a best available moneyline price of 1.32 — an implied probability of roughly 73.3%.

The Oklahoma Sooners, meanwhile, come in as pronounced underdogs at 4.00, carrying an implied chance of just 26.7% .

That gap is reinforced by the point spread. The market is pricing Texas at -8 (odds of 1.96) to -7.5 (1.92), meaning the Longhorns are expected to win by better than a touchdown-and-a-point.

Flip it around and Oklahoma is getting +7.5 (1.92) or +8 (1.92) — a number that will tempt bettors who believe the chaos of a rivalry game tends to compress margins no matter what the form book says.

On the scoring side, the total sits at a relatively modest 39 to 39.5 points. At the 39-point line, the over is priced at 1.91 and the under at 1.94; bump it to 39.5 and you'll find the over at 1.92 against an under of 1.95.

That's a number suggesting a game expected to be decided by defense and field position as much as by fireworks — a nod, perhaps, to the grinding, physical nature these rivalry contests so often take on.

The numbers tell a consistent story, and it's hard to argue with the shape of them: Texas is the better-backed team, and the -8 spread reflects genuine separation. But rivalry football rarely honors the chalk cleanly.

Expect the Longhorns to assert themselves and ultimately take care of business — the moneyline value sits firmly with them — but anticipate Oklahoma making it a fight deep into the second half. A Texas win is the smart call, though the Sooners covering the +8 would surprise no one who understands what this game means.

Projected outcome: Texas Longhorns to win, in a tighter contest than the spread suggests.
